item.description: Anglo American's proposed $54 billion merger with Canada's Teck Resources and the sale of its Brazilian nickel business have become test cases for navigating geopolitical complexities as they await antitrust approval, CEO Duncan Wanblad said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Kumwenda-Mtambo, Nelson Banya
item.content:encoded: Anglo American's (AAL.L) proposed $54 billion merger with Canada's Teck Resources (TECKb.TO) and the sale of its Brazilian nickel business have become test cases for navigating geopolitical complexities as they await antitrust approval, CEO Duncan Wanblad said on Wednesday. The Anglo-Teck merger, announced in 2025, has received approval from all countries where the companies operate except China. Both expect the deal to close by March 2027. Critical minerals have become a flashpoint in global competition, with major economies seeking to secure supply chains for electric vehicles, renewable energy and defence. China's antitrust regulator has asked Anglo American to [USN:L6N45K17B TEXT:"commit to supplying"] the country with a steady flow of copper concentrate as a condition for approving the merger, three people aware of the development said. Geopolitical shifts, supply chain disruptions and critical mineral nationalism have created a complex environment for such deals, Wanblad told a mining conference in Johannesburg via video link. 'IN NEW WATERS' "We are in new waters. We are pioneering in a way. I genuinely don't think from an antitrust perspective there should be any issues with any of these deals," Wanblad said. He cited Anglo's proposed sale of its Brazilian [USN:L1N45T0P4 TEXT:"nickel business"] to MMG (1208.HK) , which drew a [USN:L8N4581HK TEXT:"warning"] from the European Union over concerns the Hong Kong-listed miner could divert supply away from Europe, hurting stainless steel producers there. The sale is awaiting EU approval. Anglo American also agreed to sell its steelmaking coal mines in Australia to UK-based miner Dhilmar for up to $3.88 billion. "We are kind of the guinea pigs for the market in terms of working this out," Wanblad said. Wanblad also said he was hopeful the sale of diamond company De Beers would be completed by the end of this year. The sale of the assets is part of Anglo's restructuring aimed at focusing on copper and iron ore. The Teck merger would expand Anglo's copper portfolio, positioning it as the fifth-largest producer of the metal critical to the energy transition.

item.title: Muere Maricarmen Abascal, octogenaria símbolo de las protestas por la vivienda en España
item.description: Maricarmen Abascal, la mujer de 87 años cuyo desahucio desencadenó las protestas por la vivienda en España, ha muerto, informó el miércoles el sindicato de inquilinos de Madrid.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Maricarmen Abascal, la mujer de 87 años cuyo desahucio desencadenó las protestas por la vivienda en España, ha muerto, informó el miércoles el sindicato de inquilinos de Madrid. [USN:L6N45F0OT TEXT:"El desahucio"] de Abascal desencadenó una serie de [USN:L6N45P04B TEXT:"protestas"] en toda España durante las últimas dos semanas, entre las que se incluyen acampadas de activistas en una de las principales plazas de Madrid y llamados para hacer frente a la creciente crisis de la vivienda. Esas protestas, junto con el rechazo por parte de legisladores la semana pasada de los decretos destinados a frenar los desahucios y limitar la subida de los alquileres, llevaron al presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, a convocar [USN:L6N45R0A1 TEXT:"elecciones anticipadas"] para el 29 de noviembre. Ángel Víctor Torres, ministro de Política Territorial de España, lamentó la noticia y afirmó que Maricarmen se había convertido en un símbolo de lo que les estaba sucediendo a muchas familias, personas mayores y jóvenes que luchan por conseguir una vivienda propia o por conservarla.

item.title: Anglo American amenaza con cerrar su explotación de níquel en Brasil si la UE bloquea la venta a MMG
item.description: La minera británica Anglo American probablemente cerrará su explotación de níquel en Brasil si las autoridades de competencia de la UE bloquean su venta a MMG , dirá su director de operaciones a las autoridades reguladoras en una audiencia a puerta cerrada el jueves, según unas declaraciones preparadas a las que Reuters tuvo acceso.
item.dc:creator: Yun Chee Foo
item.content:encoded: La minera británica Anglo American (AAL.L) probablemente cerrará su explotación de níquel en Brasil si las autoridades de competencia de la UE bloquean su venta a MMG (1208.HK) , dirá su director de operaciones a las autoridades reguladoras en una audiencia a puerta cerrada el jueves, según unas declaraciones preparadas a las que Reuters tuvo acceso. El director de operaciones de Anglo American Brasil, Rubén Fernandes, y Cristina Morgan, directora financiera de la empresa en Brasil, intentarán convencer a la Comisión Europea de que el acuerdo de 500 millones de dólares con MMG no perjudicará a los productores europeos de acero inoxidable. La Comisión, el organismo regulador de la competencia de la UE, advirtió el mes pasado que MMG podría desviar el suministro de Europa en detrimento de sus productores de acero inoxidable. El caso se da en un contexto de preocupación de la UE por la dependencia del bloque respecto a China en materia de minerales críticos. "La prolongada revisión regulatoria ya ha provocado una considerable incertidumbre a nivel local, pero las consecuencias de que la CE prohíba la venta del negocio serían muy preocupantes", dirá Fernandes a los reguladores. "Teniendo en cuenta que MMG es el único comprador creíble que hemos identificado, y dado nuestro compromiso de abandonar nuestro negocio del níquel hace más de dos años, no tendremos más remedio que optar por un régimen de 'cuidado y mantenimiento' como vía hacia el cierre en caso de que la Comisión prohíba la venta a MMG", afirmará. Según el discurso preparado, explicará a los reguladores que es posible encontrar una solución práctica que responda a las preocupaciones de la UE. Morgan subrayará las credenciales de MMG como comprador creíble que seguirá prestando servicio a los clientes en Europa. "MMG (...) cuenta con un historial que demuestra que es un operador responsable y que ofrece un valor tangible a cambio de la inversión", afirmará por su parte Morgan. El director general ejecutivo de relaciones corporativas de MMG, Troy Hey, también estará presente en la audiencia para defender las ventajas del acuerdo ante altos funcionarios y juristas de la Comisión.

item.title: Oregon head coach Dana Altman retires in surprise move
item.description: Oregon head coach Dana Altman announced his retirement Wednesday after 16 seasons with the Ducks' program in a move that was effective immediately.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Oregon head coach Dana Altman announced his retirement Wednesday after 16 seasons with the Ducks' program in a move that was effective immediately. The decision by the winningest head coach in program history comes less than three weeks before the season opener against Stanford and ahead of next week's home exhibition game against Seattle. Altman's Oregon teams advanced to the NCAA Tournament nine times, including a 2017 run to the Final Four. He departs with a 382-182 record with the Ducks that includes four Pac-12 regular-season titles and four Pac-12 Tournament titles. "I have had to make two really tough decisions in my coaching career," Altman said in a news release. "The first was leaving Creighton, a place my family and I dearly loved, to come to Oregon. This is the second. I've loved every minute of coaching here, and stepping away is difficult and truly painful. "I love coaching, it's what I know best and what I've been fortunate enough to do for almost five decades. I'm going to miss my coaches, my players and our incredible fans more than I can express." The Ducks were 25-10 during their first season in the Big Ten Conference in 2024-25 and advanced to the second round of the NCAA Tournament. But they went 12-20 last season to finish with a sub-.500 record for the first time under Altman. Altman, 68, has served as a Division I coach for 37 seasons, going a combined 792-425 in a run that included stints at Marshall (1989-90), Kansas State (1990-94) and Creighton (1994-2010). His teams have advanced to 17 total NCAA Tournaments. Oregon announced that assistant coach Tony Stubblefield will take over on an interim basis. Stubblefield was on Altman's original staff at Oregon in 2010 before departing to become head coach at DePaul for three seasons then returning to the Ducks in 2024. "Tony has been on Dana's staff for most of his time in Eugene and knows this program as well as anyone," Oregon athletic director Rob Mullens said. "Our student-athletes know him and trust him, and he is the right person to lead the Ducks this season." Oregon announced an intention to conduct a national search for a head coach following the upcoming season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Tanzania gold mine deaths at centre of case against London accreditor of refiners
item.description: The alleged fatal shootings of two illegal artisanal miners, identified only as ZZZ and ZZY, at Tanzania's North Mara gold mine are at the heart of a lawsuit against the London Bullion Market Association that began in London on Wednesday, court documents from both sides showed.
item.dc:creator: Polina Devitt
item.content:encoded: The alleged fatal shootings of two illegal artisanal miners, identified only as ZZZ and ZZY, at Tanzania's North Mara gold mine are at the heart of a lawsuit against the London Bullion Market Association that began in London on Wednesday, court documents from both sides showed. The six-week trial is [USN:L8N45G21X TEXT:"testing"] whether the LBMA, an industry body, can be held responsible for [USN:L8N45E0YH TEXT:"alleged human rights abuses"] linked to gold supply chains. The LBMA rejects the claim. The claimants said the LBMA did not control the Tanzanian police but argued this does not preclude a duty of care with regard to the supply chain. The claimants said in the court documents the two young men were self-employed artisanal miners and farmers who supplemented their income through unlicensed, illegal mining. According to the claimants, both were shot by police while fleeing the mine in separate incidents in 2019 and neither posed a threat. Representatives of Tanzania's police did not respond to requests for comment. The claimants argue the deaths were part of a wider pattern of excessive force against local residents entering the mine in search of gold-bearing material. The LBMA, meanwhile, points to North Mara's long history of large-scale incursions by illegal miners, sometimes involving hundreds or even thousands of people. Court documents say trespassers have at times carried machetes. In ZZZ's case, the claimants say he had left his panga, or machete, at home and was unarmed when police opened fire. In ZZY's case, relatives and witnesses allege he was shot in the back while running away, court documents say. They also reject an illegality defence, saying trespassers do not lose the protection of common law and that any use of force must remain reasonable. The LBMA, however, highlights what it describes as evidential gaps. In court filings, it says the claimants have not sought incident records or reports from the Tanzanian police, citing concerns over reprisals, and have not produced medical evidence or post-mortem reports to support key allegations surrounding the deaths.

item.title: Formula One statistics for the Singapore Grand Prix
item.description: Formula One statistics for the Singapore Grand Prix at the Marina Bay street circuit, round 17 of the championship:
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Formula One statistics for the Singapore Grand Prix at the Marina Bay street circuit, round 17 of the championship: Lap distance: 4.927km. Total distance: 305.337km (62 laps) 2025 pole position: George Russell (Britain) Mercedes one minute 29.158 seconds 2025 winner: Russell Race lap record: Lewis Hamilton (Britain) Ferrari 1:33.808 (2025) Start time: 1200 GMT (2000 local) SINGAPORE Singapore hosts the sixth and last sprint race of the season on Saturday, with only one practice session on Friday. It is the first time a sprint has been held at the circuit. Sunday's night race is one of the season's most demanding physical challenges. Drivers can lose several kilos of weight during the race through sweating in the heat and humidity. The grand prix will be the 17th in Singapore since the first in 2008. Six active drivers have won -- Fernando Alonso (2008, 2010), Hamilton (2009, 2014, 2017, 2018), Sergio Perez (2022), Carlos Sainz (2023), Lando Norris (2024) and Russell (2025). Mercedes have won five times, Red Bull and Ferrari four each. Hamilton has been on pole four times. The race has been won from pole position 11 times. The lowest winning grid position is 15th for Alonso in a now-notorious 2008 race in which Brazilian teammate Nelson Piquet crashed his Renault deliberately on team orders. The 2024 race, with only two retirements, was a rarity for Singapore with no safety car deployment. The safety car deployment probability is around 80%. There are 19 corners, making the track one of the twistiest along with Monaco. A one-stop strategy is the most likely. CHAMPIONSHIP Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli leads teammate Russell by 84 points. Ferrari's Hamilton is third and 106 points off the pace while teammate Charles Leclerc is fourth and 129 behind Antonelli. Mercedes are 151 points clear of Ferrari in the constructors' standings. RACE WINS Six drivers have won races this season. Antonelli has won eight, including five in a row early on. Russell has won three, Norris two, Hamilton, Leclerc and Verstappen one apiece. Antonelli won in China, Japan, Miami, Canada, Monaco, Belgium, Italy and Spain, Russell in Australia, Austria and Azerbaijan. Norris won in Hungary and the Netherlands, Hamilton took his first win since 2024 with victory in Barcelona and Leclerc won in Britain. Verstappen won the Bahrain GP in Malaysia. Mercedes have won 11 of 16 races. Hamilton has a record 106 career victories from 396 starts and with three teams. Verstappen has won 72 grands prix and is third on the all-time list behind Hamilton and Michael Schumacher (91). POLE POSITION Mercedes have been on pole in all but five grands prix this season — Russell in Australia, Canada, Barcelona, Austria and Azerbaijan, Antonelli in China, Japan, Miami, Monaco, Britain and Belgium. Norris was on pole in Hungary, the Netherlands and Spain. Alpine's Pierre Gasly took pole in Italy and Verstappen in Malaysia. Hamilton has had a record 104 career poles, his most recent in Hungary in 2023. MILESTONE Verstappen is starting his 250th grand prix this weekend. Verstappen's win in Malaysia ensured the Dutch driver has won at least once in every season since he joined the Red Bull Racing team in 2016.

item.title: Em Atenas, Rubio associa valores da Grécia Antiga ao lema “America First”
item.description: O secretário de Estado dos Estados Unidos, Marco Rubio, instou as nações ocidentais nesta quarta-feira a abraçarem os valores da Grécia Antiga de “heroísmo, honra e dever”, associando esses ideais à agenda “America First” do presidente Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Landay
item.content:encoded: O secretário de Estado dos Estados Unidos, Marco Rubio, instou as nações ocidentais nesta quarta-feira a abraçarem os valores da Grécia Antiga de “heroísmo, honra e dever”, associando esses ideais à agenda “America First” do presidente Donald Trump. “Hoje em dia, tornou-se moda acreditar que uma política externa esclarecida significa priorizar a comunidade global em detrimento do próprio povo”, disse Rubio a autoridades gregas, diplomatas e outros convidados. Com as ruínas do Partenon ao fundo, ele argumentou que os homens da Grécia Antiga “sabiam que não havia nada de egoísta ou errado na lealdade à própria nação”. Possível candidato à indicação republicana para suceder Trump em 2028, Rubio proferiu o discurso no Pnyx, onde outrora se reunia a assembleia de cidadãos da Atenas Antiga. O discurso de Rubio ecoou o discurso do vice-presidente JD Vance na Conferência de Segurança de Munique, em fevereiro de 2025, que apresentou os desafios da Europa como um afastamento dos valores ocidentais compartilhados e gerou críticas dos líderes do continente. Isso foi seguido pela Estratégia de Segurança Nacional de Trump, de novembro de 2025, que alertou que a Europa enfrentava o “apagamento da civilização” devido à migração e aos desafios à soberania nacional. “Hoje, nos encontramos em uma encruzilhada, pois a próxima década e as decisões que tomarmos escreverão a história do próximo século”, disse Rubio. “O rumo que tomarmos determinará se o Ocidente manterá seu lugar à frente do mundo ou se resignará a um futuro de atrofia, servidão e declínio.” “Sob o governo do presidente Trump, os Estados Unidos fizeram sua escolha”, acrescentou Rubio. “Optamos pela busca sem remorso do poder nacional.” Rubio faz uma visita a três aliados europeus da Otan como parte de uma viagem que começou na Islândia. Na manhã desta quarta-feira, Rubio e seu homólogo grego reafirmaram os estreitos laços entre os EUA e a Grécia nas áreas de segurança, energia e comércio. Ele encerra a viagem com conversas com autoridades portuguesas na quinta-feira, em Lisboa.

item.title: Russell’s title hopes on the line as F1 heads to Singapore
item.description: Formula One arrives in Singapore this week with George Russell's title challenge hanging by a thread after his retirement in Malaysia handed Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli firm control of the championship battle.
item.dc:creator: Rohith Nair
item.content:encoded: Formula One arrives in Singapore this week with George Russell's title challenge hanging by a thread after his retirement [USN:L1N45Q023 TEXT:"in Malaysia"] handed Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli firm control of the championship battle. The Marina Bay Street Circuit has a history of delivering drama under the lights, and Russell desperately needs some luck to go his way after a [USN:L4N45Q017 TEXT:"power unit failure"] while running third at Sepang allowed Antonelli to stretch his advantage to 84 points. Russell had arrived in Malaysia buoyed by a dominant victory in Azerbaijan and would have hoped to reinforce his title credentials before his car failed with five laps remaining. With little time to rest as Formula One heads into the final leg of its triple-header on the streets of Singapore, Russell faces a very different challenge as he looks to keep his slim title hopes alive. ENGINE SETBACK FOR RUSSELL The Briton won last year's race at the Marina Bay Street Circuit but is [USN:L6N45S0MC TEXT:"set to start from the back of the grid"] on Sunday after Mercedes confirmed he had no engines left in his season's allocation of four. Russell will need a new engine for the sprint weekend and had hoped to take the penalty at the US Grand Prix in Austin, where overtaking is easier than the tight and slow Singapore track where 11 of the 16 races have been won from pole. The 4.927-km-long Singapore circuit features 19 corners with walls so close they punish even the smallest errors while heat and humidity make it one of the season's most physically demanding races. "George has the added challenge of a power unit penalty, which will mean starting from the back of the grid on Sunday, following the engine failure in Malaysia," Mercedes boss Toto Wolff said. "That is particularly frustrating given the way he drove last weekend and the result he deserved to be fighting for. "Unfortunately, these things are part of the sport and our focus now is on giving him the best possible car and opportunities to fight back through the field." Antonelli's objective is far simpler. The Italian finished a distant fifth last year - more than half-a-minute behind Russell - but he does not need a victory. As the season draws to a close, all he needs to do is keep Russell behind him and avoid handing momentum back to his team mate. 'UNFINISHED BUSINESS' FOR VERSTAPPEN For Red Bull's Max Verstappen, Malaysia was more than just his first victory of the season. Red Bull had spent much of the year looking like a team waiting for opportunities rather than creating them, but at Sepang the pieces came together as the car had the pace to compete with the Mercedes duo at the top of the standings. Verstappen seized pole position and, when the rain came, was untouchable in the treacherous conditions as he delivered Red Bull's first victory with their own power unit. However, Singapore offers the first chance to discover whether Malaysia was an isolated return to form or the beginning of something more significant. Marina Bay is not Sepang and the demands of the circuit are almost entirely different. "I think the win was quite track-specific so we will need to see how we go heading into this week," Verstappen said. "I enjoy this track as a street circuit, it has a lot of corners and is quite bumpy. The heat is obviously a factor but at least we are racing at night this time around. "Singapore is a race that I haven't won before, so it does feel like unfinished business at this track."

item.title: Tortuga de 194 años, el animal terrestre más viejo, podría ofrecer pistas para una vida más larga
item.description: El animal terrestre más viejo que se conoce en el mundo, una tortuga gigante de Aldabra llamada Jonathan, cuya edad se estima en unos 194 años, podría deber su extraordinaria longevidad a una combinación de rasgos genéticos y a su capacidad para mantener el funcionamiento de sistemas celulares clave de una forma más juvenil, según científicos.
item.dc:creator: Marta Serafinko
item.content:encoded: El animal terrestre más viejo que se conoce en el mundo, una tortuga gigante de Aldabra llamada Jonathan, cuya edad se estima en unos 194 años, podría deber su extraordinaria longevidad a una combinación de rasgos genéticos y a su capacidad para mantener el funcionamiento de sistemas celulares clave de una forma más juvenil, según científicos. Se sabe que los ejemplares de esta especie viven más de 100 años, pero Jonathan ha superado con creces esa cifra. Llevada a la remota isla de Santa Elena, en el Atlántico Sur, ya adulta en 1882 —probablemente procedente del atolón de Aldabra o de las Seychelles graníticas—, la tortuga reside ahora en un recinto de Plantation House, la casa del gobernador. "Se ha afirmado que otras tortugas de Aldabra han vivido tanto como Jonathan, pero él es el que cuenta con más pruebas documentales que respaldan su edad", dijo Benjamin Vaisvil, investigador afiliado a la organización Kallel y coautor principal del estudio publicado el miércoles en la revista Science Advances. Los científicos han estudiado a Jonathan para desentrañar los secretos de la asombrosa longevidad de este animal, secuenciando su genoma y analizando su epigenoma, los marcadores químicos que controlan qué genes se activan y cuáles se desactiva. "Hemos encontrado cambios en el genoma de Jonathan en vías asociadas a la longevidad, como la reparación del ADN, la función mitocondrial, la regulación de la insulina y la función de los telómeros", explicó Vaisvil. Las mitocondrias son estructuras consideradas la central energética de la célula. La insulina es una hormona que ayuda a regular los niveles de azúcar en sangre al permitir que esta entre en las células del cuerpo para obtener energía. Los telómeros son capuchones protectores situados en los extremos de los cromosomas, estructuras que contienen información genética en el interior de los núcleos celulares. Los investigadores compararon el epigenoma de Jonathan con el de otras cuatro tortugas de Aldabra, que abarcaban desde ejemplares jóvenes hasta adultos mayores. Mientras fingían darle de comer a Jonathan, esperaron a que empezara a morder el aire; entonces, le mantuvieron la boca abierta con una mano enguantada y le rasparon debajo de la lengua con un kit especializado. Las autoridades de Santa Elena restringen las extracciones de sangre para prevenir riesgos de infección. Para explicar el hallazgo, Vaisvil comparó el genoma con un cuaderno de recetas y el epigenoma con notas manuscritas en los márgenes. "A medida que el cuaderno de recetas envejece, esas notas se vuelven más difíciles de leer con claridad. Podemos considerar eso como la entropía de metilación", dijo Vaisvil, refiriéndose a una medida del desorden en un determinado proceso bioquímico. La mayoría de las anotaciones del cuaderno de Jonathan parecen muy antiguas. Sin embargo, en determinadas regiones —tramos de ADN que actúan como interruptores que controlan si los genes se activan o se desactivan—, la entropía de metilación de Jonathan era inferior a la de todas las tortugas estudiadas, excepto la de un ejemplar joven de 5 años. Estas regiones controlan genes que influyen en la longevidad. Los investigadores identificaron 287 genes con variantes exclusivas de Jonathan, entre ellos algunos relacionados con la supresión tumoral y la reparación del ADN. La tortuga también posee copias adicionales de un gen que codifica una proteína que persigue a las células envejecidas y cancerosas. "GIGANTE AMABLE" Cuando era más joven, Jonathan era conocido por sus travesuras, como volcar sillas y tumbarse sobre bolas de croquet, según Joe Hollins, veterinario de toda la vida de la tortuga y coautor del estudio. Desde entonces, las cataratas le han dejado prácticamente ciego. Hollins describe hoy a Jonathan como "un gigante gentil". Determinar cuánto tiempo pueden vivir las tortugas gigantes es complicado, ya que los registros históricos fiables son escasos y muchas de ellas sobreviven a los investigadores. El registro de datos antes del siglo XX también resultaba problemático. Si bien la edad de una tortuga joven puede estimarse a partir de los anillos de crecimiento en las placas que forman el caparazón del animal, determinar la edad de los adultos es más difícil. El nuevo estudio se centró únicamente en una tortuga excepcionalmente longeva, lo que dificulta determinar si los rasgos identificados son exclusivos de Jonathan o comunes entre las tortugas de larga vida. "No podemos afirmar con certeza que lo que hemos descubierto sea la razón de su longevidad", señaló Vaisvil. Es posible que también hayan contribuido factores ambientales. Jonathan vive en una isla tropical, con una dieta óptima cuidadosamente supervisada por veterinarios especializados. Los resultados de la investigación coinciden en líneas generales con los patrones documentados en estudios sobre personas de vida excepcionalmente larga, lo que sugiere que algunos mecanismos del envejecimiento podrían ser comunes a todas las especies. Vaisvil señaló que un estudio reciente sobre una mujer de 117 años reveló una función mitocondrial inusualmente eficiente, lo que concuerda con los hallazgos en algunas de las regiones de Jonathan.

item.title: Microsoft incorpora más inteligencia artificial a los PC en su desafío a Apple
item.description: Microsoft presentó el miércoles un modelo de programación basado en inteligencia artificial que puede ejecutarse directamente en computadores personales, así como una nueva tecnología de seguridad para impedir que los agentes de IA accedan a datos sin autorización, lo que supone un reto a una iniciativa similar de Apple .
item.dc:creator: Stephen Nellis
item.content:encoded: Microsoft (MSFT.O) presentó el miércoles un modelo de programación basado en inteligencia artificial que puede ejecutarse directamente en computadores personales, así como una nueva tecnología de seguridad para impedir que los agentes de IA accedan a datos sin autorización, lo que supone un reto a una iniciativa similar de Apple (AAPL.O) . La empresa de software también presentó un nuevo portátil equipado con los chips de Nvidia (NVDA.O) , en su intento por convertir Windows en una plataforma para que los agentes de IA realicen tareas como escribir código sin tener que acceder a la nube. Microsoft anunció el lanzamiento de Microsoft Execution Containers, una herramienta destinada a impedir que los agentes accedan a datos y realicen tareas no autorizadas cuando se ejecutan en un portátil o un computador de escritorio. Anthropic, OpenAI y Nvidia usarán las herramientas, dijo Pavan Davuluri, vicepresidente ejecutivo de Windows y dispositivos, en el evento celebrado en San Francisco. "Necesitábamos convertir el computador de escritorio en el lugar más seguro para que los agentes ejecuten sus tareas", dijo Satya Nadella, presidente ejecutivo de Microsoft. Davuluri explicó que las nuevas herramientas permitirían a los departamentos de TI establecer normas para los agentes y que el sistema operativo Windows se encargaría de hacer cumplir dichas normas en el computador de cada empleado. Para Microsoft, esta iniciativa supone una apuesta por que parte del trabajo que actualmente se realiza en sus costosos centros de datos de computación en la nube de Azure pueda trasladarse a potentes equipos Windows en empresas y hogares, un mercado en el que la empresa mantiene una posición dominante. Se trata de una oportunidad de mercado que su rival Apple también está persiguiendo con los nuevos ordenadores Mac. Para Nvidia, abrirse paso en el mercado de los ordenadores con Windows podría ayudarla a conquistar uno de los últimos grandes mercados dominados por Intel (INTC.O) y Advanced Micro Devices (AMD.O) . El evento, que Microsoft presentó como una actualización de su sistema operativo Windows y de su línea de hardware Surface, fue la culminación de años de trabajo entre el fabricante líder de sistemas operativos para PC y Nvidia, la empresa de chips de IA, con el objetivo de llevar muchas tareas —como escribir código informático o abordar proyectos empresariales complejos— directamente a los computadores de escritorio y portátiles gracias a los chips RTX Spark de Nvidia. Nadella y el presidente ejecutivo de Nvidia, Jensen Huang, subieron al escenario para presentar el Surface Laptop Ultra, como se denomina el nuevo dispositivo.

item.title: Parte dos ministros de Comércio do G20 denuncia excesso de capacidade industrial em declaração
item.description: Ministros do Comércio de vários países do G20, juntamente com a União Europeia e a Polônia, aderiram a uma declaração liderada pelos EUA que clama por medidas para eliminar o excesso estrutural de capacidade fabril e as políticas “não mercadológicas” que incentivam a superprodução, informou na quarta-feira o gabinete do Representante de Comércio dos EUA.
item.dc:creator: David Lawder
item.content:encoded: Ministros do Comércio de vários países do G20, juntamente com a União Europeia e a Polônia, aderiram a uma declaração liderada pelos EUA que clama por medidas para eliminar o excesso estrutural de capacidade fabril e as políticas “não mercadológicas” que incentivam a superprodução, informou na quarta-feira o gabinete do Representante de Comércio dos EUA. A declaração conjunta -- que não contou com a adesão do Brasil -- foi acordada por representantes seniores dos países à margem de uma reunião do Comitê de Comércio da OCDE. Uma reunião liderada pelos EUA com os ministros do Comércio do Grupo dos 20, realizada em Milwaukee na semana passada, não conseguiu chegar a um consenso sobre o tema do excesso de capacidade industrial. “Exortamos todos os países a tomarem medidas para eliminar o excesso estrutural de capacidade e produção em suas economias, inclusive por meio do fim do uso de políticas e práticas não mercadológicas que distorcem os mercados e contribuem para o problema”, afirmaram os ministros do Comércio na declaração. “Observamos que, na ausência de tais medidas, um número crescente de países está tomando medidas para defender suas indústrias, trabalhadores e economias contra as distorções resultantes dessas políticas e práticas.” A declaração foi assinada pelos ministros do Comércio da Argentina, Austrália, Canadá, União Europeia, França, Alemanha, Índia, Itália, Japão, Coreia do Sul, México, Polônia, Turquia, Reino Unido e Estados Unidos. Notavelmente ausentes da declaração conjunta estavam os membros do G20 China, Brasil, Indonésia, Rússia, Arábia Saudita e África do Sul. A declaração afirma que o excesso estrutural de capacidade e produção leva à superprodução, desestimula o investimento baseado no mercado e prejudica as exportações baseadas no mercado, distorcendo preços e padrões de produção e impedindo a concorrência. O representante comercial dos EUA, Jamieson Greer, há muito argumenta que o excesso estrutural de capacidade na China, alimentado por subsídios estatais, levou a uma enxurrada de exportações chinesas que estão pressionando as indústrias nacionais em todas as regiões. A China rejeitou as alegações de que suas políticas industriais tenham criado excesso de capacidade e acusa os países ocidentais de usar a questão para justificar medidas protecionistas. Greer afirmou em comunicado que não é surpreendente que países afetados por déficits comerciais crescentes ou que sentissem outras pressões devido às exportações impulsionadas pelo excesso de capacidade tivessem se comprometido com uma ação coletiva. “O sistema comercial global está completamente desequilibrado, e o presidente Trump está corrigindo isso com parceiros que compartilham da mesma visão”, acrescentou.

item.title: Zealand, Roche's obesity drug helps patients lose up to 9.2% weight in mid-stage trial
item.description: Zealand Pharma said on Wednesday its experimental drug helped people who are overweight or obese and have type 2 diabetes lose up to 9.2% of their body weight in a mid-stage trial. The Danish company is developing it with Roche .
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Zealand Pharma (ZELA.CO) said on Wednesday its experimental drug helped people who are overweight or obese and have type 2 diabetes lose up to 9.2% of their body weight in a mid-stage trial. The Danish company is developing it with Roche (ROPC.S) . The 220-patient trial met its main goal, with patients taking the once-weekly petrelintide losing between 7.4% and 9.2% body weight after 28 weeks, depending on the dose, versus 2% with placebo Petrelintide lowered HbA1c by as much as 0.65%, while levels of the blood sugar measure rose 0.23% among patients receiving placebo, Zealand said About 1.9% of patients taking petrelintide discontinued treatment because of gastrointestinal side effects, compared with 1.7% of those on placebo Most gastrointestinal side effects were mild and occurred while doses were being increased, Zealand said Roche gained access to petrelintide through a collaboration and licensing deal worth up to [USN:TUA29MGZN TEXT:"$5.3 billion"] last year, giving it shared development rights to the therapy that mimics amylin, a hormone co-secreted with insulin The companies have started late-stage testing in about 7,000 people — with and without type 2 diabetes and those with established cardiovascular disease

item.title: Lula reclama de campanha "aquém da minha possibilidade" em fala transmitida por engano pelo PT
item.description: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) reclamou da sua campanha no primeiro turno em fala transmitida por engano pelo PT durante um encontro com parlamentares atuais e eleitos da aliança petista, ecoando o que lideranças dos partidos já haviam destacado em reuniões ao longo desta semana, após a eleição de domingo em que Lula terminou o primeiro turno atrás de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL).
item.dc:creator: Lisandra Paraguassu
item.content:encoded: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) reclamou da sua campanha no primeiro turno em fala transmitida por engano pelo PT durante um encontro com parlamentares atuais e eleitos da aliança petista, ecoando o que lideranças dos partidos já haviam destacado em reuniões ao longo desta semana, após a eleição de domingo em que Lula terminou o primeiro turno atrás de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). “Acho que nós fizemos uma campanha aquém da minha possibilidade, poderíamos ter feito mais. Disse para o Edinho (Silva, presidente do PT) que essa foi a campanha menos organizada que participei desde 1989”, disse Lula na fala, que não era para ter sido transmitida, mas foi vazada nas redes do PT. A fala de Lula repete o diagnóstico feito pela Executiva do partido e por líderes aliados em duas reuniões esta semana sobre as dificuldades da campanha. Presidente do partido e coordenador da campanha, Edinho foi o principal alvo das reclamações do que foi considerada uma campanha sem rumo e equivocada. Na terça-feira, durante a reunião da Executiva, Edinho teve que se ausentar durante um momento, mas disse aos presentes para continuarem a conversa. Os membros, no entanto, suspenderam até sua volta porque “Edinho precisava ouvir o que eles tinham a falar”, disse um dos presentes. Na reunião desta quarta, que reuniu vários parlamentares jovens e muitos com grande engajamento nas redes sociais, como André Janones e Ana Elisa Silva - influenciadora eleita deputada federal por Minas Gerais com mais de meio milhão de votos - Lula foi cobrado pela dificuldade do partido em usar as redes. A avaliação principal foi de que Lula ganhou nas ruas, mas perdeu nas redes. Também em uma reunião com equipes de campanha e governadores e senadores, eleitos e derrotados, o presidente já tinha ouvido a mesma cobrança. Ele fez um mea culpa. “Eu tenho que falar nas redes, no celular. Eu não uso celular porque tenho a mão para fazer outras coisas. Eu gosto de falar só o essencial. Mas o pessoal me enche o saco. ‘Faz uma selfie’. Eu não gosto, mas hoje eu resolvi fazer”, disse. De fato, pela manhã, Lula postou pela primeira vez um vídeo no estilo selfie. Ele também admitiu uma decepção da população com seu terceiro mandato. “Uma das expectativas do povo era que o Lula 3 repetisse o Lula 2. Todo mundo comprou um carrinho, um televisor, mas é importante lembrar que depois que eu deixei a Presidência em 2010, nunca mais o Brasil cresceu acima de 3%”, afirmou. Desde o resultado eleitoral de domingo, quando terminou 2,2 milhões de votos atrás de Flávio, Lula tem se concentrado em participar de reuniões em Brasília, além de gravar programas eleitorais, e a única agenda pública marcada até agora é apenas no sábado, no Rio Grande do Norte.

item.title: Canadian dollar weakens as risk-off sentiment drives markets
item.description: The Canadian dollar weakened against its US counterpart on Wednesday as a downturn in risk appetite helped drive broad-based gains for the greenback and investors weighed minutes from the Federal Reserve's latest meeting.
item.dc:creator: Fergal Smith
item.content:encoded: The Canadian dollar weakened against its US counterpart on Wednesday as a downturn in risk appetite helped drive broad-based gains for the greenback and investors weighed minutes from the Federal Reserve's latest meeting. The loonie was trading 0.3% lower at 1.4255 per US dollar, or 70.15 US cents, after moving in a range of 1.4207 to 1.4280. On Monday, the currency touched an 18-month low at 1.4293 as the greenback benefited from safe-haven demand. "It's not anything CAD specific," said Amo Sahota, director at Klarity FX in San Francisco. "This is risk-off sentiment, and the loonie is getting mopped up into that as well." The [USN:L6N45T0TN TEXT:"US dollar"] rose against a basket of major currencies as renewed pressure on French bonds due to fiscal concerns weighed on the euro . Stocks on [USN:L6N45T0YS TEXT:"Wall Street"] pulled back from record highs. [USN:L6N45T0TQ TEXT:"Fed policymakers"] were divided last month over the rationale for raising interest rates, with "some participants" seeing a hike as needed to keep the impact of energy and other price shocks at bay, but a more hawkish core viewing it as necessary to guard against emerging demand-driven inflation. The price of oil, one of Canada's major exports, gave back its earlier gains. US crude oil futures were trading 1.4% lower at $88.20 a barrel. Canadian employment data for September, due on Friday, could help guide expectations for Bank of Canada interest rate hikes. Economists expect a jobs gain of 9,200 and the unemployment rate to edge up to 6.5% from 6.4% in August. Canadian government bond yields were mixed across the curve. The 10-year was up 1.1 basis points at 3.939% after earlier touching a six-day high at 4.008%.

item.title: Syria weighs military aid for Saudi Arabia amid Yemen war, sources say
item.description: Syria is carefully considering providing military assistance to key ally Saudi Arabia amid an escalating war against the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen, a US official and a Syrian military official briefed on the matter said.
item.dc:creator: Timour Azhari
item.content:encoded: Syria is carefully considering providing military assistance to key ally Saudi Arabia amid an escalating war against the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen, a US official and a Syrian military official briefed on the matter said. Options being considered include defensive aid to protect the kingdom from attacks, or deployment of forces in an offensive capacity to help Saudi-backed Yemeni troops fight the Houthis, the sources said. The US official said Saudi Arabia had requested that Syria deploy forces to fight the Houthis. In response to a request for comment to the Syrian foreign ministry, a Syrian diplomat said Syria stood firmly with Saudi Arabia in the face of Houthi attacks but that the government's primary focus was on domestic priorities such as recovery from the country's civil war. "Should Saudi Arabia request any military cooperation or exchange of expertise, this would take place exclusively through official channels and within the framework of the bilateral agreements governing relations between our two brotherly countries," the diplomat said in a statement. The Saudi government media office and Yemen's information minister did not respond to requests for comment. Saudi Arabia has been requesting assistance far and wide, from [USN:L6N45308G TEXT:"the US"] to Europe and the Middle East, for both defensive and offensive support in a [USN:L6N3Y307N TEXT:"renewed war"] against the group that follows weeks of Houthi missile and drone attacks on the kingdom. The war is being led on the ground by a patchwork of Yemeni government forces with Saudi air support. They have made [USN:L1N45T00S TEXT:"limited advances"] since the campaign was launched on Monday. Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa made a public visit to Riyadh on Tuesday and met Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, also known as MbS. He discussed potential Syrian military assistance for the kingdom, among other matters, the US official said. Footage broadcast by Syrian state media showed that he was escorted back to his plane by Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman, a brother of the crown prince who has overseen the Yemen file. DEPLOYMENT COULD DEEPEN TENSIONS WITH NEIGHBOURS Syrian fighters from opposition groups that battled former leader Bashar al-Assad in the country's civil war have in past years been recruited as mercenaries for other conflicts, notably Libya's internal conflict and the Russia-Ukraine war. But for Damascus, any potential deployment carries risks. The militias that made up the armed opposition are now under the nascent Syrian state, which has adopted a policy of avoiding engagement in conflict, including the Iran war , to focus on recovery from the 14-year Syrian civil war. The state is still piecing together its army from the various militia groups from the former rebel coalition that toppled Assad, which included many hardline Sunni Islamist and foreign fighters, and trying to contain tensions with minorities including the Alawites, a Shi'ite offshoot to which Assad belonged. A conflict between that army and the Houthis, who are also adherents of an offshoot of Shi'ite Islam, could have divisive religious undertones that the Syrian leadership and its Western partners want to avoid, the US official said. It is for this reason that it previously rejected a [USN:L8N40204O TEXT:"US request"] to help fight Hezbollah in Lebanon. Involvement in a battle against the Iran-backed Houthis could also be viewed as a hostile act by Iran and its allies Hezbollah in Lebanon and militias in Iraq, with which the Syrian rebels-turned-rulers have a history of conflict. KEEN TO SHOW SUPPORT At the same time, Sharaa is keen to show the country's support for Saudi Arabia and MbS, who played a decisive role helping the former jihadist gain international legitimacy, including by brokering a May 2025 meeting between Sharaa and US President Donald Trump. Saudi Arabia has also provided financial assistance to Syria and a Syrian show of support could result in that increasing, the US official said. "A new Syria sending defensive personnel of a very small number to the most holy places in the Islamic world, alongside technical support to neutralise incoming drones, would be tremendously and positively symbolic," said H.A. Hellyer, senior associate fellow at the Royal United Services Institute in London. "But anything beyond, particularly in terms of Syrian boots on the ground, I think would be a wholly different proposition, and one I think Damascus would avoid, given the priorities they need to focus on in Syria," he said.

item.title: Elliott and Siris explore $2 billion-plus Gigamon sale, sources say
item.description: Elliott Investment Management and Siris are exploring a sale of Gigamon that could value the infrastructure software provider at more than $2 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Milana Vinn
item.content:encoded: Elliott Investment Management and Siris are exploring a sale of Gigamon that could value the infrastructure software provider at more than $2 billion, according to people familiar with the matter. The firms have tapped investment bankers at Bank of America (BAC.N) and Perella Weinberg Partners (PWP.O) to advise Gigamon on the process, which is in its early stages, said the people, who requested anonymity because the deliberations are confidential. A sale process could attract interest from private equity firms as well as strategic buyers seeking to expand their capabilities in network monitoring, cybersecurity and cloud infrastructure management, the people said. Based in Santa Clara, California, Gigamon provides software that helps companies monitor network traffic and detect security threats. Founded in 2004, the company serves more than 4,000 customers globally, including banks, healthcare providers and government agencies, according to its website. Gigamon generated more than $400 million in annual recurring revenue and around $170 million in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA), the sources said. Gigamon, Siris, Elliott, and Bank of America declined to comment. Perella Weinberg did not respond to a request for comment. Elliott acquired Gigamon in 2017 in a take-private transaction, which valued the company at about $1.6 billion. Private equity firm Siris bought a minority stake in Gigamon in 2024. The potential sale comes as investors continue to show interest in software companies that provide critical infrastructure tools underpinning cloud computing, cybersecurity and artificial intelligence deployments.

item.title: Flórida pede a tribunal que obrigue Meta a alterar Facebook e Instagram para adolescentes
item.description: A Flórida solicitou nesta quarta-feira a um juiz estadual que ordenasse mudanças no Instagram e no Facebook para proteger melhor os jovens usuários, dando continuidade a uma ação judicial que acusa a controladora Meta de causar danos a adolescentes, após a maioria dos Estados ter resolvido reclamações semelhantes por meio de um acordo abrangente.
item.dc:creator: Diana Jones
item.content:encoded: A Flórida solicitou nesta quarta-feira a um juiz estadual que ordenasse mudanças no Instagram e no Facebook para proteger melhor os jovens usuários, dando continuidade a uma ação judicial que acusa a controladora Meta (META.O) de causar danos a adolescentes, após a maioria dos Estados ter resolvido reclamações semelhantes por meio de um acordo abrangente. Em um pedido apresentado a um tribunal do condado de Pasco, o procurador-geral da Flórida, James Uthmeier, solicitou uma liminar temporária obrigando a Meta a identificar e remover dessas plataformas os usuários menores de 14 anos residentes no Estado, limitar o tempo de uso dos adolescentes a duas horas por dia em todos os aplicativos e desativar recursos como reprodução automática e rolagem infinita para eles. O pedido solicitou que as mudanças fossem implementadas imediatamente e permanecessem em vigor enquanto o processo judicial segue adiante. Um porta-voz da Meta não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário. A ação judicial da Flórida contra a Meta, que acusa a empresa de projetar conscientemente suas plataformas para serem viciantes para jovens usuários e de enganar os consumidores quanto à sua segurança, foi uma das dezenas de ações semelhantes movidas por Estados em todo o país. Em agosto, a Meta chegou a acordos com 48 dos outros Estados e com a capital Washington, concordando em pagar até US$18 bilhões e fazer alterações para os usuários adolescentes de suas plataformas. A Meta afirmou que se empenha para manter os adolescentes seguros em suas plataformas, e a empresa negou qualquer irregularidade ao concordar com o acordo. O valor total do pagamento representa cerca de três a quatro meses de lucro e cerca de um mês de receita para a Meta. Uthmeier, um republicano, optou por não aderir ao acordo e dar continuidade à sua ação judicial. A Flórida afirmou no processo que o acordo equivalia a uma “mera reprimenda, será visto cinicamente como o custo de se fazer negócios e, de qualquer forma, não impedirá que esse tipo de comportamento se repita no futuro”. As mudanças solicitadas na petição de Uthmeier são mais rigorosas do que aquelas com as quais a empresa concordou como parte do acordo, pois cortariam o acesso dos adolescentes às mensagens após o atingimento dos limites de tempo e impediriam a empresa de exibir anúncios para eles. As mudanças que a Meta concordou em fazer como parte do acordo são uma indicação de que essas alterações são possíveis, argumentou o escritório de Uthmeier.

item.title: Ata do Fed mostra autoridades divididas quanto à lógica por trás do aumento dos juros em setembro
item.description: Os formuladores de política monetária do Federal Reserve estavam divididos no mês passado quanto aos fundamentos para o aumento das taxas de juros, com “alguns participantes” considerando o aumento necessário para conter o impacto dos choques nos preços da energia e outros choques de preços, enquanto um grupo via a medida como necessária para proteção contra a inflação emergente impulsionada pela demanda.
item.dc:creator: Howard Schneider
item.content:encoded: Os formuladores de política monetária do Federal Reserve estavam divididos no mês passado quanto aos fundamentos para o aumento das taxas de juros, com “alguns participantes” considerando o aumento necessário para conter o impacto dos choques nos preços da energia e outros choques de preços, enquanto um grupo via a medida como necessária para proteção contra a inflação emergente impulsionada pela demanda. Os argumentos opostos foram descritos na ata da reunião do banco central dos EUA realizada em 15 e 16 de setembro, na qual o Fed votou por unanimidade pelo aumento de 0,25 ponto percentual na taxa básica de juros, mesmo com as autoridades discordando se a medida era essencialmente preventiva ou representava uma mudança para uma política monetária significativamente mais restritiva, destinada a conter investimentos e gastos. Essa divisão, aliada às diferentes interpretações sobre a situação atual da economia, prenuncia um debate provavelmente acirrado na reunião de política monetária de 27 e 28 de outubro sobre se a inflação assumiu uma dimensão mais ampla, impulsionada pela demanda, que justifique novas medidas do Fed neste momento. A alternativa seria adiar novos aumentos da taxa para observar se os dados futuros indicam que os choques nos preços da energia, das tarifas e outros choques de preços estão diminuindo e que a inflação está voltando à meta de 2% do banco central. “Muitos participantes enfatizaram que uma trajetória mais elevada para a faixa-alvo seria prudente do ponto de vista da gestão de riscos, servindo como garantia contra a inflação permanecer persistentemente acima da meta devido a uma demanda mais forte do que o esperado ou a novos choques adversos de oferta”, afirmou a ata da sessão, divulgada nesta quarta-feira. Outros, por sua vez, consideraram a “taxa de juros mais alta” aprovada em setembro importante para impedir que os recentes choques de energia e outros choques de preços tivessem uma influência mais ampla sobre os preços, enquanto “alguns” justificaram seu apoio ao aumento como uma adequação ao que consideravam uma taxa de juros neutra estimada mais elevada. “Vários participantes afirmaram que consideravam a taxa de juros atual não restritiva ou apenas levemente restritiva”, indicou a ata. “A maioria dos participantes avaliou que outro aumento na faixa-alvo para a taxa de fundos federais provavelmente seria apropriado até o final do ano.” Os investidores, que nos dias seguintes à reunião de setembro esperavam aumentos sucessivos da taxa, reduziram desde então suas apostas e agora acreditam que o Fed manterá sua taxa de juros na faixa de 3,75% a 4,00% em sua reunião no final deste mês, pouco antes das eleições legislativas de meio de mandato, mas que fará um novo aumento na reunião de 8 e 9 de dezembro. Após a divulgação de dados de emprego e inflação mais fracos do que o esperado, os comentários recentes de autoridades do Fed reforçaram a percepção de que os formuladores de política monetária agora concederiam algum tempo para que novos dados mostrassem se a inflação subjacente estaria recuando dos níveis atuais — que estão mais de um ponto percentual acima da meta do Fed — ou se se mostraria mais persistente. No entanto, os argumentos apresentados na reunião de setembro persistiram, com algumas autoridades monetárias também afirmando que consideram necessários aumentos de juros mais frequentes e mais rápidos, o que pode levar a um resultado dividido e a várias dissidências na reunião no final deste mês.

item.title: Las minutas de la Fed muestran una división sobre la justificación de la subida de tasas
item.description: Los responsables de la política monetaria de la Reserva Federal estuvieron divididos el mes pasado respecto de los motivos para subir las tasas de interés, mostraron el miércoles las minutas de la última reunión del banco central.
item.dc:creator: Howard Schneider
item.content:encoded: Los responsables de la política monetaria de la Reserva Federal estuvieron divididos el mes pasado respecto de los motivos para subir las tasas de interés, mostraron el miércoles las minutas de la última reunión del banco central. "Algunos participantes" consideraron que el alza era necesaria para contener el impacto de las perturbaciones de los precios de la energía y otros factores, mientras que un núcleo más "duro" la vio como imprescindible para protegerse de una inflación emergente impulsada por la demanda. Los argumentos contrapuestos quedaron reflejados en la minuta de la reunión del banco central estadounidense del 15 y 16 de septiembre, en la que la Fed votó por unanimidad a favor de subir la tasa de interés oficial un cuarto de punto porcentual, pese a que los responsables monetarios no se pusieron de acuerdo sobre si la medida era principalmente preventiva o si representaba un giro a un sesgo más restrictivo para frenar la inversión y el gasto. La división, junto con las diferentes interpretaciones sobre la situación actual de la economía, presagia un debate probablemente intenso en la reunión del 27 y 28 de octubre sobre si la inflación ha adquirido una dimensión más amplia, impulsada por la demanda, que justifique nuevas medidas de la Fed en este momento. La alternativa sería esperar antes de aplicar nuevas subidas de tasas para ver si los datos que se publiquen muestran que las perturbaciones en los precios de la energía, los aranceles y otros factores están remitiendo y que la inflación vuelve al objetivo del 2% del banco central. "Muchos participantes hicieron hincapié en que una trayectoria al alza del rango objetivo sería prudente desde el punto de vista de la gestión de riesgos, ya que serviría de garantía si la inflación se mantiene persistentemente sobre el objetivo debido a una demanda más fuerte de lo esperado o a nuevas perturbaciones adversas en la oferta", se indicó en el acta de la sesión, publicada el miércoles. Otros, por su parte, consideraron que la "subida de la tasa de interés oficial" aprobada en septiembre era importante para evitar que las recientes perturbaciones en el sector energético y de otro tipo tengan una influencia más amplia en los precios, mientras que "un par" de ellos justificaron su apoyo argumentando que se ajustaba a lo que consideraban una tasa de interés neutral más alta. "Varios participantes señalaron que consideraban que la tasa de interés oficial actual no era restrictiva o lo era solo ligeramente", según las minutas. "La mayoría de los participantes estimó que probablemente sería adecuado otro aumento del rango objetivo de la tasa de los fondos federales antes de que finalice el año".

item.title: Anglo American threatens to close Brazilian nickel operation if EU blocks sale to MMG
item.description: British mining company Anglo American will likely shut down its Brazilian nickel operation if EU antitrust regulators block its sale to Hong Kong-listed mining and metals company MMG , its chief operating officer will warn regulators at a closed hearing on Thursday, according to prepared comments obtained by Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Yun Chee Foo
item.content:encoded: British mining company Anglo American (AAL.L) will likely shut down its Brazilian nickel operation if EU antitrust regulators block its sale to Hong Kong-listed mining and metals company MMG (1208.HK) , its chief operating officer will warn regulators at a closed hearing on Thursday, according to prepared comments obtained by Reuters. Anglo American Brazil COO Ruben Fernandes and Cristina Morgan, the company's chief financial officer in Brazil, will seek to convince the European Commission that the $500 million deal with MMG will not hurt European stainless steel producers. The Commission, which is the EU antitrust watchdog, had last month [USN:L8N4581HK TEXT:"warned that MMG may divert the supply away from Europe"] to the detriment of its stainless steel producers. The case comes amidst EU concerns about the bloc's reliance on China for critical minerals. "The protracted regulatory review has already caused considerable uncertainty locally, but the consequences of the EC prohibiting the sale of the business would be very troubling," Fernandes will tell regulators, according to remarks seen by Reuters. "Recognising that MMG is the only credible buyer that we identified, and given our commitment to exit our nickel business more than two years ago, we will have little option but to head towards 'care and maintenance' as the pathway to closure in the event that the Commission prohibits the sale to MMG," he will say. According to the prepared remarks, he will tell regulators that it is possible to find a practical solution that will address the EU concerns. Morgan will underline MMG's credentials as a credible buyer who will continue to serve customers in Europe. "The selection process scrutinised the prospective bidder's operational capabilities and track record of operating responsibly, ability to develop future projects and intentions for our employees, fair value, along with the ability to fund the acquisition," she will tell the EU watchdog. "MMG is a fellow ICMM member, is well known to us and has that track record of being a responsible operator and offering deliverable value for the investment," she will say, referring to the industry body the International Council on Mining and Metals. MMG's executive general manager of corporate relations Troy Hey will also be at the hearing arguing for the merits of the deal to senior Commission officials and lawyers.

item.title: EU envoys approve new Russia sanctions listings, diplomats say
item.description: European Union envoys approved on Wednesday 1,646 new designations under the bloc's sanctions regime for Russia, with the majority focused on the country's military industrial complex, three EU diplomats said.
item.dc:creator: Julia Payne
item.content:encoded: European Union envoys approved on Wednesday 1,646 new designations under the bloc's sanctions regime for Russia, with the majority focused on the country's [USN:L1N45S0RE TEXT:"military"] industrial complex, three EU diplomats said. More than half of the newly added entities and individuals are involved in the chain of production of Russia's ballistic missiles, such as the 9M723 Iskander-M, which can only be intercepted by US-made Patriot air defence systems. Ukraine has virtually run out of these interceptors as the US military diverts resources to the Gulf, and Russia has seized on this vulnerability to ramp up [USN:L8N44V0TY TEXT:"ballistic missile"] strikes. The designations include a range of entities involved in missile testing and research as well as the production of solid fuels and rocket engines for Russia's Iskander system. The EU is also targeting producers of specialised textiles and synthetic and carbon fibres used across a range of different missile systems, one of the sources specified. In addition, the list has drone manufacturers, shipyards that service submarines and 77 Russian politicians who ran for parliamentary seats in Russian-occupied Ukrainian territories. The sanctions will be formally adopted when EU foreign ministers meet on Monday. Russian President Vladimir Putin said last week Moscow would not resume [USN:L8N45N1NG TEXT:"diesel exports"] - currently banned until the end of October - to global markets until sanctions are lifted. The global diesel market has tightened due to the Iran war, which, combined with the loss of Russian diesel after Ukrainian strikes on [USN:L6N45T0GE TEXT:"Russian refineries"], triggered shortages in Russia. The EU, concerned about strengthening links between Russia and North Korea, also added seven North Korean entities and individuals linked to Moscow's war effort. In July, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Russia struck Ukraine with [USN:L8N43W21X TEXT:"North Korean missiles"] for the first time in nearly a year after an apparent stock replenishment.

item.title: McTominay cleared to return, Napoli say
item.description: Napoli midfielder Scott McTominay has been cleared to return to action after undergoing a procedure to correct a heart arrhythmia, the Italian club said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Napoli midfielder Scott McTominay has been cleared to return to action after undergoing a procedure to correct a heart arrhythmia, the Italian club said on Wednesday. The 29-year-old Scotland international underwent a planned ablation procedure at Manchester's Spire Hospital in September after being diagnosed with a mild, benign arrhythmia. McTominay has since undergone further tests and been cleared to resume sporting activity. He has returned to training with Napoli and will be available for selection by coach Massimiliano Allegri. "Scott McTominay underwent further diagnostic tests, which showed that he is fit to play. The Napoli player therefore resumed training with the rest of the team after the period spent training separately," the club said in a statement. McTominay has not played since August 30 and missed Napoli's 3-2 Serie A defeat by champions Inter Milan as well as their Champions League loss to Arsenal. Napoli, who are ninth in the Serie A standings, host sixth-placed Frosinone on Saturday.

item.title: Trump administration plans to charge international students $70,000 for work authorization
item.description: The US Department of Homeland Security has proposed that international students pay at least $70,000 in training fees if they want to work in the country, according to a government notice posted online on Wednesday, part of the Trump administration's wider crackdown on foreign visa holders.
item.dc:creator: Susan Heavey
item.content:encoded: The US Department of Homeland Security has proposed that international students pay at least $70,000 in training fees if they want to work in the country, according to a government notice posted online on Wednesday, part of the Trump administration's wider crackdown on foreign visa holders. Under the proposal, nonimmigrant students with F-1 visas would be required to pay $70,000 to a certified institution for on-the-job training, known as Optional Practical Training (OPT), and $30,000 for any additional work training. DHS said the new rules were meant "to combat fraud, strengthen the integrity of the immigration system, and protect US workers." Under the OPT system, foreign students can engage in work training for up to 20 hours per week while school is in session, as well as for a limited time after graduation, with an additional allowance for those with degrees in science, technology, engineering and mathematics. Those who enroll are currently expected to pay around $500. "DHS is now setting a fee to ensure employers, students, and institutions are engaging in appropriate activities consistent with admission as an F-1 nonimmigrant," the agency said. Such training programs often serve as a bridge for students seeking work under H-1B visas, which the Trump administration has also targeted with increased fees . For decades, the [USN:L3N3V90SB TEXT:"H-1B program"] has allowed young engineers and scientists from across the world, especially India and China, to turn years of study at US universities into high-paying jobs and a path to permanent US residency. Leading US tech companies have come to rely heavily on these workers to fill skilled positions. When he was campaigning in 2024, President Donald Trump vowed he would make it easier for foreign students to remain in the country, suggesting they be automatically awarded a Green Card after graduation. Like similar DHS proposals, the rule change is likely to be met with swift legal challenges. "This proposed rule isn't going to fare well in the courts, just as the 100k H-1B fee and other restrictionist policies have been struck down," Doug Rand, director of the Talent Mobility Fund, which works to attract foreign STEM professionals, wrote on LinkedIn on Wednesday. The proposal is subject to 30 days of public comment before it can be finalized. DHS said it would wait 60 days after finalization before putting the rule into effect to allow schools, students and employers time to prepare.

item.title: T20 ties have softened on-field rivalries, says Harmer
item.description: South Africa spinner Simon Harmer expects none of the animosity of Australia’s last test tour to South Africa to resurface in the three-match series between the two countries, which gets underway at Kingsmead on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Africa spinner Simon Harmer expects none of the animosity of Australia’s last test tour to South Africa to resurface in the three-match series between the two countries, which gets underway at Kingsmead on Friday. Australia are playing their first test series in South Africa since the 2018 "Sandpapergate" scandal, when the tourists used sandpaper to illegally alter the condition of the ball in a bid to gain more swing, resulting in bans for captain Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft. The scandal followed a series of ugly confrontations, including off-field fighting and on-field jostling between the two teams in a sport that prides itself on its etiquette. Harmer believes the growth of Twenty20 franchise cricket, where international rivals regularly become teammates, has taken some of the sting out of such contests. "I expect Australia to come out firing and being competitive, but I think the nature of T20 cricket is such that you're playing with a lot of players, a lot of the time," he told a press conference on Wednesday. “Gone are the days where you had these huge rivalries, where you would play against one another every 18 to 24 months, and it created that sort of argy bargy on the field. “I think T20 has softened that a little bit but I don't expect Australia to be soft by any stretch of the imagination.” The 37-year-old Harmer, expected to be one of two spinners South Africa will use in the first test, said Australia were always extremely competitive and the series in South Africa would be closely fought. “They fight to the death; their lower order always seems to score a lot of runs with a never-say-die attitude. I think it is quite a similar trait to South Africans. We're resilient, and we probably do our best when our backs are up against the wall. “I think that was there for the world to see in the World Test Championship final,” Harmer said of last year’s clash at Lord’s where South Africa beat Australia by five wickets. “I think it was almost a foregone conclusion that Australia were going to win that game, but our team found a way to get through it and to get the win.”

item.title: Litigation funder Omni Bridgeway raises $1 billion
item.description: Litigation funder Omni Bridgeway said on Wednesday that it has closed a $1 billion fundraising round, increasing its assets under management to $4.2 billion.
item.dc:creator: Sara Merken
item.content:encoded: Litigation funder Omni Bridgeway said on Wednesday that it has closed a $1 billion fundraising round, increasing its assets under management to $4.2 billion. Omni Bridgeway is a global litigation funder that has been publicly listed on the Australian Securities Exchange since 2001. Funders like Omni finance lawsuits and other legal disputes in exchange for a portion of litigation proceeds The firm said it has closed the capital raise for two funds, and that nearly all of the investors in a prior round have reinvested There were 39 active commercial funders in the US market in 2025, according to a report in March by litigation finance advisory firm Westfleet Advisors, which also noted that many funders faced challenges raising money from investors Burford Capital, another large litigation funder that is publicly listed in New York and London, said last week that a [USN:L6N45K0R5 TEXT:"funding agreement"] would entitle it to about $1.4 billion of a landmark $5.7 billion patent verdict won by Taction Technology against Apple

item.title: Fed policymakers divided over rate-hike logic in September, minutes show
item.description: Federal Reserve policymakers were divided last month over the rationale for raising interest rates, with "some participants" seeing a hike as needed to keep the impact of energy and other price shocks at bay, but a more hawkish core viewing it as necessary to guard against emerging demand-driven inflation.
item.dc:creator: Howard Schneider
item.content:encoded: Federal Reserve policymakers were divided last month over the rationale for raising interest rates, with "some participants" seeing a hike as needed to keep the impact of energy and other price shocks at bay, but a more hawkish core viewing it as necessary to guard against emerging demand-driven inflation. The competing arguments were outlined in the minutes of the US central bank's September 15-16 meeting, at which the Fed voted unanimously to raise the [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"policy rate"] by a quarter of a percentage point even as officials disagreed about whether the move was largely precautionary or represented a shift towards significantly tighter monetary policy meant to curb investment and spending. The split, and the varying interpretations of where the economy stands right now, set up a likely vigorous debate at the October 27-28 policy meeting over whether inflation has taken on a broader, demand-driven dimension that warrants further Fed action now. The alternative would be to wait on further rate hikes to see if incoming data shows energy, tariff and other price shocks receding and inflation heading back to the central bank's 2% target. "Many participants emphasized that a higher path for the target range would be prudent on risk-management grounds, providing insurance against inflation remaining persistently above target due to stronger-than-expected demand or further adverse supply shocks," said the minutes of the session, which were released on Wednesday. Others, meanwhile, saw the "higher policy rate" approved in September as important to prevent recent energy and other shocks from having a broader influence on prices, while "a couple" framed their support for the hike as matching what they saw as a higher estimated neutral rate of interest. "Several participants stated that they viewed the current policy rate as not restrictive or only mildly restrictive," the minutes stated. "Most participants assessed that another increase in the target range for the federal funds rate would likely be appropriate by year end." Investors, who had expected sequential rate hikes in the days following the September meeting, have since pared back their bets and now see the Fed keeping its policy rate in the 3.75%-4.00% range at its meeting later this month, just ahead of midterm congressional elections, but hiking again at the December 8-9 gathering. Following the release of [USN:L1N45N170 TEXT:"weaker-than-expected jobs"] and [USN:L1N45M0L0 TEXT:"inflation data"], Fed officials' recent comments added weight to the sense that policymakers would now allow some time for new data to show whether underlying inflation was coming down from current levels that are more than a percentage point above the Fed's target, or proving more persistent. But the arguments outlined at the September meeting have persisted, with some policymakers also saying they feel more and faster rate hikes are needed, potentially setting up a divided outcome and multiple dissents at the meeting later this month.

item.title: Ravens acquire Pro Bowl C Cam Jurgens from Eagles
item.description: The Baltimore Ravens acquired two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens in a trade with the Philadelphia Eagles on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Baltimore Ravens acquired two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens in a trade with the Philadelphia Eagles on Wednesday. The Ravens pocketed a seventh-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft in exchange for a fifth-round selection in that same draft and a second-round pick in 2028. "Cam is a player we have long admired going all the way back to the draft process. He's a young foundational piece along our offensive line -- a great scheme and cultural fit who will contribute quickly in Baltimore. We are confident that Cam will significantly impact our team and community," Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta said in a statement. Baltimore was seeking an answer at center after All-Pro Tyler Linderbaum departed in free agency, triggering a turnstile effect at the position. Vega Ioane is the fourth player the Ravens have tried at center. The Eagles subtract Jurgens from the roster just as six-time Pro Bowl right tackle Lane Johnson announced his retirement. Johnson retired Tuesday after 14 seasons and two Super Bowl championships. Johnson, 36, who missed Sunday's loss against the Los Angeles Rams for personal reasons, said he wants to focus on his mental health. "We weren't looking to move Cam," Eagles general manager Howie Roseman said. "Obviously, the Ravens have been looking for a center. ... Kind of told them wasn't anything we were looking to do. Over the last 24 hours, it got to the point where we felt like it could be a win-win for them. Obviously, getting a player who's been a two-time Pro Bowl center and obviously for us, being able to get the picks we're able to get, and use that money also to sign players. Had a chance to watch Drew (Kendall) here play center is doing a nice job. Have a young player there. "... I think for us, when you talk about the two and the five, moving from the seventh to the fifth. We've had success in the fifth round, plus the money, plus with Drew playing, we felt like we were getting four players for one, and just felt like for us, you know, with all these guys that we got coming up, a lot on the defensive side of the ball that we want to re-sign and want to extend, felt like that was a good situation." Jurgens, who has played both guard and center, is expected to make his Ravens debut next week against the Cleveland Browns because he is currently in concussion protocol. Jurgens, 27, took over for the retired Jason Kelce and played in 20 regular-season and playoff games (19 starts) during the Eagles' run to a title in Super Bowl LIX. Signed to a four-year, $68 million extension in 2025, Jurgens started all four games this season and 45 of the 62 in which he has appeared since Philadelphia drafted him in the second round out of Nebraska in 2022. The Ravens shuffled Ioane from guard to center for last Sunday's 24-18 victory over the Tennessee Titans. Vegas was selected 14th overall in this year's draft out of Penn State. Center Jovaughn Gwyn sustained a fractured fibula in Baltimore's 34-31 win over Dallas on Sept. 27 and is expected to miss two to three months. The Ravens also lost center Ethan Pocic in the victory over the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro due to a long-term knee injury. Baltimore already was without center Danny Pinter, expected to be the opening-week starter, to a season-ending knee injury in training camp. --Field Level Media

item.title: Rahm's lawyer tells court Spaniard is done with LIV Golf after three seasons
item.description: Former world number one Jon Rahm is quitting LIV Golf, robbing the breakaway circuit of one of its biggest stars while it fights to emerge from Chapter 11 bankruptcy.
item.dc:creator: Frank Pingue
item.content:encoded: Former world number one Jon Rahm is quitting LIV Golf, robbing the breakaway circuit of one of its biggest stars while it fights to emerge from Chapter 11 bankruptcy. Rahm's attorney John Beck told a bankruptcy hearing on Wednesday that the two-times major champion made his decision after looking over details of LIV Golf's planned next phase. "Mr. Rahm has independently reviewed the proposed terms of LIV 2.0, as the parties have been referring to it, and has determined that those terms are unacceptable as to him, and he will not be participating going forward in LIV 2.0," Beck told the court. Other golfers asked a US bankruptcy judge to help terminate their contracts and clarify their ability to negotiate with other tournament organizers and sponsors as their LIV contracts go unpaid. LIV has already agreed to terminate Sergio Garcia’s contract after determining that the league would not honour its terms, and attorneys for Bryson DeChambeau, Cameron Smith, An Byeong-hun, Marc Leishman, Cameron Tringale and Matthew Wolff asked the judge to allow those players out of their old contracts. Ending those contracts would not preclude those players from agreeing to participate in LIV 2.0. According to sources with knowledge of league operations, conversations with players regarding their participation in LIV Golf 2.0 remain on track, and statements made in court today do not change the trajectory, timeline, or momentum of the transaction.
