Rahm, one of the most high-profile players to join LIV Golf, has won three consecutive season-long individual titles on LIV since joining the circuit in late 2023, eight months after winning the Masters for his second major title. When [USN:L4N4501M7 TEXT:"LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 protection"] in New Jersey last month, its filing listed several star golfers as creditors still owed millions in unsecured claims. Among them, Rahm had the largest claim among players at $7.5 million. Earlier this week [USN:L4N45R1JA TEXT:"LIV secured funding"] from BC Partners to help it emerge from restructuring and strengthen its financial footing ahead of the 2027 season. The financing, up to $300 million, remains subject to bankruptcy court approval and customary conditions. BC Partners Credit, which provides financing to middle-market companies, said the funding would support what it described as the next phase of LIV Golf, under which players would become equity owners of both the league and its teams.

item.title: CDC sees low plague risk, monitors Siberia arrivals after worker death, director says
item.description: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Director Erica Schwartz said on Wednesday the risk to the US from an unconfirmed pneumonic plague case in Siberia was extremely low, but the agency was prepared to monitor and screen travelers.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Director Erica Schwartz said on Wednesday the risk to the US from an unconfirmed pneumonic plague case in Siberia was extremely low, but the agency was prepared to monitor and screen travelers. "We are working with Department of Homeland Security, working (with) Department of State, Department of War, and other agencies within the government to make sure that we know exactly if anyone from that area comes into the United States," Schwartz said at the Wall Street Journal's The Future of Health event in Washington. The CDC has a port health station at the John F. Kennedy International Airport that can conduct surveillance and screening for travelers from the region entering the United States, she added. The US Department of Health and Human Services did not immediately respond to a request for comment on whether the agency planned to set up screening at JFK. An HHS spokesman said there are about 200 individuals per year from the Siberian region who travel to the United States. Direct flights between Russia and the United States have been suspended since the start of the Ukraine war in 2022. Russia's health regulator said there were [USN:SPN43X00F TEXT:"no risks"] of an epidemic breaking out in Siberia after a plague institute worker there died from pneumonia of an as-yet unestablished origin, in a case that has prompted international concern. "What we're doing from a whole of government standpoint is we're making sure that we understand exactly what that threat is," Schwartz said. "We are very confident that the threat to the United States is extremely low." US President Donald Trump also [USN:S0N42W01I TEXT:"told reporters"] he does not think the death is from a bioweapon.

item.title: Florida asks court to force Meta to change Facebook, Instagram for teens
item.description: Florida asked a state judge on Wednesday to order changes to Instagram and Facebook to better protect young users, pressing ahead with a lawsuit accusing parent Meta Platforms of harming teens after most states resolved similar claims through a sweeping settlement.
item.dc:creator: Diana Jones
item.content:encoded: Florida asked a state judge on Wednesday to order changes to Instagram and Facebook to better protect young users, pressing ahead with a lawsuit accusing parent Meta Platforms (META.O) of harming teens after most states resolved similar claims through a sweeping settlement. In a filing in a Pasco County court, Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier asked for a temporary injunction forcing Meta to identify and remove users in the state under the age of 14 from those platforms, limit teens there to two hours a day across all apps and turn off features like autoplay and infinite scroll for them. The filing asked that the changes be implemented immediately and be in place while the lawsuit moves forward. A Meta spokesperson in a statement said after the company's settlement with nearly every other state, Florida should focus on getting other platforms to take action. "The attorney general should be using taxpayer resources to get YouTube and TikTok to empower parents and protect teens in Florida. We regret that he has chosen instead to pursue a meritless preliminary injunction years into the litigation," the spokesperson said. Florida's lawsuit against Meta, which accuses the company of knowingly engineering its platforms to be addictive for young users and misleading consumers about its safety, was one of dozens of similar lawsuits filed by states across the country. In August, Meta [USN:L6N44N0VA TEXT:"reached settlements"] with 48 of the other states and Washington, DC, agreeing to pay up to $18 billion and make changes for teen users of its platforms. Meta has said it works hard to keep teens safe on its platforms, and the company denied wrongdoing in agreeing to settle. The total payout represents about three to four months of profit and about one month of revenue for Meta. Uthmeier, a Republican, opted not to join the settlement and proceed with his lawsuit. Florida said in the filing that the settlement amounted to a “mere slap on the wrist, will be cynically viewed as the cost of doing business, and in any event will not prevent this kind of behavior going forward.” The changes Uthmeier's filing seeks are more stringent than those the company agreed to as part of that settlement, as they would cut off teens' access to messaging after their time limits are hit and bar the company from showing them advertisements. The changes Meta agreed to make as part of the settlement are an indication these changes are possible, Uthmeier's office argued.

item.title: Tropical Storm Isaias forecast to hit US Gulf coast as hurricane early Saturday
item.description: Tropical Storm Isaias formed in the Gulf of Mexico on Wednesday and is forecast to strengthen into a hurricane before slamming into the southern US coast early on Saturday, the National Hurricane Center said.
item.dc:creator: Brad Brooks
item.content:encoded: Tropical Storm Isaias formed in the Gulf of Mexico on Wednesday and is forecast to strengthen into a hurricane before slamming into the southern US coast early on Saturday, the National Hurricane Center said. The storm is forecast to pass through areas with significant [USN:L1N45T0JO TEXT:"offshore oil and gas production"], along with onshore refining facilities, which could pressure inventories and already-high prices at the pump. About 11.2 million barrels of oil production could be lost across the Gulf through the duration of the storm, a marked increase from the 7.1 million barrels impacted by [USN:FWN42P0ED TEXT:"Tropical Storm "]Bertha in July, according to a model forecast from consulting firm Earth Science Associates. The NHC expects Isaias to develop into a hurricane by Thursday as it quickly picks up power over the warm Gulf waters before making landfall early Saturday, most likely somewhere along the Mississippi, Alabama or Florida Panhandle coast. The storm was located about 500 miles south of the Louisiana coast early Wednesday. Isaias could produce isolated rainfall amounts of 10 inches across parts of the Gulf Coast, stretching from Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle, the NHC said in its latest bulletin. The storm could also produce 3 inches or more of rain further inland, with the NHC warning that "flash and urban flooding, along with isolated river flooding, will be possible" across the Southeast. Isaias is expected to run into strong upper-level winds, known as vertical wind shear, in the final 24 hours before it reaches the northern Gulf Coast, which could weaken the storm. Still, the NHC says that it's “looking more likely that Isaias will be a significant hurricane when it reaches the coast.” Asked about the storm on Wednesday, President Donald Trump , who is due to attend a college football game in Alabama on Saturday, told reporters in the Oval Office, "I hadn't heard about a hurricane. ... that's not good."

item.title: US FDA expands use of Novartis drug for chronic skin condition
item.description: The US Food and Drug Administration has expanded the use of Novartis' drug to treat adults with a chronic skin condition that causes recurring itchy welts, the Swiss drugmaker said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US Food and Drug Administration has expanded the use of Novartis' (NOVN.S) drug to treat adults with a chronic skin condition that causes recurring itchy welts, the Swiss drugmaker said on Wednesday. The condition, called symptomatic dermographism, is a form of chronic hives in which scratching, rubbing or friction on the skin can trigger itchy welts. The approval adds to momentum for the drug, remibrutinib, which investors have increasingly focused on after [USN:L8N45008E TEXT:"recent late-stage failures of the company's"] cholesterol drug pelacarsen and muscle-wasting disease therapy del-desiran increased scrutiny of its pipeline. Remibrutinib, branded as Rhapsido, is the first FDA-approved treatment specifically for adults with symptomatic dermographism whose symptoms are not adequately controlled with antihistamines, Novartis said. The approval expands the drug's use beyond chronic spontaneous urticaria, another common form of chronic hives for which it is already approved in the United States. In the late-stage study, 29.3% of patients taking remibrutinib achieved complete resolution of hives after 12 weeks, compared with 14% of patients receiving placebo. Patients receiving remibrutinib began showing improvements as early as two weeks after starting treatment, the company said. Novartis said the drug's safety profile was consistent with earlier studies, with the most common side effects including nasal congestion, sore throat, headache, nausea and abdominal pain. The approval follows [USN:L1N44T094 TEXT:"positive late-stage trial results for remibrutinib"] in relapsing multiple sclerosis, a disease in which the immune system attacks the nervous system.

item.title: Trump threatens to fire political advisers if their interests conflict
item.description: President Donald Trumpsaid on Wednesday he would fire two top election advisers if their work for a Bosnian territorial government posed a conflict of interest weeks ahead of critical US elections, then concluded that it did not.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson, Jarrett Renshaw, Steve Holland
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump said on Wednesday he would fire two top election advisers if their work for a Bosnian territorial government posed a conflict of interest weeks ahead of critical US elections, then concluded that it did not. The two advisers, Chris LaCivita and James Blair, traveled to the self-governing territory of Republika Srpska in Bosnia and Herzegovina ahead of [USN:L6N45Q01G TEXT:"elections there"] on Sunday, according to a New York Times report on Tuesday. The newspaper said Republika Srpska's government retained and paid them to advise on voting issues. Trump was caught off guard by the Republican duo's trip at a critical time in US domestic politics and was angered, a Trump ally familiar with internal White House dynamics said on Wednesday. "Chris LaCivita and James Blair are outside consultants," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform. "I do not have any idea who else they work for but will, on reflection, ask them and, if there’s a conflict, I will terminate them, immediately!" Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office later, Trump said, "They don't have a conflict." The statement signaled a potential rift between a Republican president fighting to maintain slim congressional majorities in the November 3 midterm elections and the pair of advisers he had charged with leading outside campaign operations. LaCivita and Blair did not immediately respond to a request for comment about the president's post. The White House also did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The United States, Russia and the European Union have been vying for influence over Bosnia. In April, Trump called Blair "one of the brightest political minds in the Country" in a social media post as he stepped away from his role as White House deputy chief of staff. At the time, the president said Blair would work "to prepare Republicans to DEFY LONGSTANDING HISTORY AND WIN the Midterms." Since then, he has overseen Trump's outside political funding arm, MAGA Inc., that has raked in hundreds of millions of dollars to boost Republican candidates nationwide. But even with a Republican cash advantage over Democrats, the map of competitive US Senate and US House races continues to expand, threatening Republican majorities in both chambers. LaCivita, a Marine veteran, is a well-known Republican strategist who helped lead Trump's 2024 presidential campaign.

item.title: Christa Pike 'angry and confused' about Tennessee's failed execution effort, lawyers say
item.description: Christa Pike, sentenced to death for a 1995 murder, awoke "angry and confused" in a hospital this week with a long recuperation ahead after surviving Tennessee's botched effort to execute her, her lawyers said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Allen
item.content:encoded: Christa Pike, sentenced to death for a 1995 murder, awoke "angry and confused" in a hospital this week with a long recuperation ahead after surviving Tennessee's botched effort to execute her, her lawyers said on Wednesday. A week ago, Pike, 50, was taken from the execution chamber to a Nashville hospital, unconscious, critically ill and with severe arm injuries after two injections of the caustic barbiturate pentobarbital [USN:L1N45N0VS TEXT:"failed to kill her"] at the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution. As late as Monday, her lawyers believed Pike was brain dead and that life support would be removed the next day following the second botched execution in Tennessee this year, which has renewed scrutiny of capital punishment in the US . "But on Tuesday, to the shock of everyone, including me, including her team, and including the medical team, Christa woke up and began talking," Randall Spivey, one of her lawyers, told reporters after a court hearing on Wednesday, where a judge ordered Tennessee officials to preserve syringes and other evidence from the botched execution. "She is angry and confused about everything right now," Spivey said. "She is very aware that the state tried to execute her." Governor Bill Lee has suspended all executions for the rest of the year while investigators look into the botched executions of Pike and of Tony Carruthers in May, when prison officials were unable to set up intravenous lines. Pike remains very sick and shackled to her hospital bed, facing a long road to recovery, her lawyers said. She cannot swallow or eat, has pneumonia, cannot move her "tremendously swollen" hands or arms, and it is unclear if she will regain her lost mobility, they said. Although she still has "cognitive confusion," the lawyers said, she has been speaking with those around her. "She has wanted to know what's happened, and she's asked about several people," Spivey said. "She's asked about the victim's family." Pike was sentenced to death for her role as a teenager in the 1995 torture and murder of her 19-year-old schoolmate Colleen Slemmer. She is the first person known to have survived a "completed execution attempt" in the US, her lawyers say, calling it a violation of the Constitution's prohibition on cruel and unusual punishments. A UNIQUE CASE Pike's lawyers are unexpectedly continuing their litigation against state officials, seeking to pierce the secrecy that normally surrounds execution procedures in Tennessee and other states. Earlier on Wednesday, a judge in Davidson County Chancery Court, I'Ashea Myles, agreed to order Tennessee officials to preserve all evidence from the failed execution, including syringes, drug packaging and lot numbers, catheters, intravenous lines and gurney restraints. The all-female execution team requested by Pike used at least seven needles during a grueling ordeal that lasted more than two hours, and one needle was bent 90 degrees when it was pulled out, her lawyers said. Myles largely sided with Pike's lawyers at the end of Wednesday's hearing, describing the litigation, which began in January in an effort to prevent the scheduled execution, as unusual because no one had anticipated Pike surviving. "This case is unique, to say the least," Myles said. She also ordered the state to preserve internal communications about the attempted execution, including incident reports, witness accounts and encrypted messages. She has yet to rule on a request by Pike's lawyers that the Tennessee Department of Correction let them take any residual traces of the execution drugs for chemical analysis. The Tennessee Department of Correction has opposed what it says is a "duplicative and unnecessary" preservation order, arguing it is already legally required to preserve all evidence and that it was already willing to share most, if not all, of what Pike's lawyers sought. Tennessee and other US states have long struggled to acquire execution drugs. They cannot be obtained from major pharmaceutical companies because of a European trade ban on companies that sell products for use in torture or executions. Tennessee, like other states, has turned to small, largely unregulated compounding pharmacies to make small batches of the drugs, promising to hide their identity. "Today's hearing was about transparency, about why Christa, the courts, the media and the public should not simply take the state's word about what happened last Wednesday," Luke Ihnen, another lawyer for Pike, told reporters after the judge's ruling. He repeated the demand that Tennessee Governor Bill Lee commute Pike's sentence to life in prison and never attempt to execute her again. A spokesperson for Lee, who denied a clemency appeal two days before the failed execution, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Pike's lawyers had sought an alternative to lethal injections, saying her small veins and related medical conditions made her afraid that something would go wrong.

item.title: The status of Iran's uranium enrichment programme
item.description: US Vice President JD Vance told Reuters on Monday that Iran must make a "meaningful" reduction in its uranium enrichment capacity to satisfy US demands and end the countries' seven-month war.
item.dc:creator: Francois Murphy
item.content:encoded: US Vice President JD Vance [USN:L6N45T01N TEXT:"told Reuters on Monday"] that Iran must make a "meaningful" reduction in its uranium enrichment capacity to satisfy US demands and end the countries' seven-month war. The Trump administration has sought to force Iran to denuclearize in slow-moving negotiations to end the conflict. Below is a summary of what is known, and not, about the current status of Iran's uranium enrichment programme, which is at the heart of its nuclear infrastructure. WHAT DID IRAN HAVE BEFORE THE US AND ISRAEL BOMBED? Israel launched airstrikes on Iran's nuclear facilities on June 13 of last year, soon followed by the United States. In a 12-day campaign, they destroyed or badly damaged the three uranium-enrichment facilities that were known to be operating in Iran at the time. They argued that Iran was getting too close to being able to produce a nuclear weapon, but the UN nuclear watchdog, the International Atomic Energy Agency, said it had no credible indication of a coordinated weapons programme. Iran was, however, enriching uranium to up to 60% purity, a short step from the roughly 90% of weapons grade. The IAEA, which had access to all Iran's declared nuclear sites, including its enrichment plants, until the US-Israeli bombing campaign, estimates Iran had 440.9 kg of uranium enriched to up to 60% when the first bombs fell. That is enough, if enriched further, for 10 nuclear weapons, according to an IAEA yardstick. Iran also had stocks of uranium enriched to lower levels. No other country has enriched uranium to such a high level without producing nuclear weapons. The US and its European allies say there is no civil justification. The IAEA said the enrichment level and quantity produced were of serious concern. Iran has long held that it does not want and is not seeking to develop nuclear weapons. WHAT REMAINS? Iran has not told the IAEA how much of its enriched uranium survived the attacks or informed it of its whereabouts. It has also not let IAEA inspectors return to the bombed sites since they were attacked. Of the three enrichment plants, the only above-ground one, at the sprawling Natanz nuclear facility, was destroyed, the IAEA has said. The other two, at Natanz and Fordow, were at least badly damaged and are widely believed to be out of action. The day before Israel attacked, Iran informed the IAEA it was opening a new enrichment plant at Isfahan, which diplomats say is in a network of tunnels there that appears largely unscathed by US bombing. The IAEA says it does not know the status of that plant or whether it contains nuclear material. While some of Iran's enriched uranium will have been destroyed in the US-Israeli strikes, IAEA chief Rafael Grossi [USN:L1N3ZX0VL TEXT:"said in March"] his agency believes "a bit more than 200 kg" of Iran's uranium enriched to up to 60% remains in the tunnel complex at Isfahan, with some also still at Natanz. WHERE DOES THAT LEAVE IRAN'S ENRICHMENT CAPACITY? Not even Iran's arch-foe Israel alleges Iran is currently enriching uranium. How long it would need to restart is an open question, but as long as a significant portion of its 60% stock remains, it could in principle enrich to weapons grade with relatively little effort and few machines known as centrifuges. A 2015 deal between Iran and major powers gave the IAEA extra inspection powers, including oversight of the number of centrifuges and parts for them. US President Donald Trump's withdrawal from that deal in 2018 prompted its collapse and the IAEA lost track of those machines. Their current number and whereabouts is unknown. WHAT DID VANCE SAY ABOUT IRANIAN ENRICHMENT? In an interview with Reuters, Vance questioned why Iran had 60% enriched uranium if it claims to not desire nuclear weapons. And he positioned meaningful reductions in "enrichment capacity" as a prerequisite to satisfying US demands and ending the war. "Sixty percent enriched uranium, you know, I'm hardly a nuclear scientist, but I've learned this: you don't need that for any energy production. You don't need it for anything except to have threshold weapons-grade uranium," Vance said. "I think if they want to show a commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, they would do something meaningful on their enrichment capacity. So far, we haven't seen a long-term commitment to do that." THEN HOW CAN IRAN REDUCE ITS CAPACITY? Given that Iran is not currently known to be enriching, any reduction is likely to be compared to its previous capacity, which was significant. A reduction could refer to purity, output or the number of enrichment sites.

item.title: Saudi Arabia launches air safety probe into flydubai incident, sources say
item.description: Saudi Arabia has launched an air accident probe following last week's cockpit stabbing on a flydubai jet, as experts examine any fallout for aviation safety alongside a separate UAE-led criminal investigation, three people close to the matter said.
item.dc:creator: Allison Lampert, Tim Hepher, Steven Scheer, Federico Maccioni
item.content:encoded: Saudi Arabia has launched an air accident probe following last week's [USN:S8N44D013 TEXT:"cockpit stabbing on a flydubai jet"], as experts examine any fallout for aviation safety alongside a separate UAE-led criminal investigation, three people close to the matter said. Safety probes designed to keep flights safe are normal after accidents but are not mandatory when a deliberate act is involved, such as the suspected attempt by a co-pilot to bring down the Israel-bound flydubai jet on September 30. Until now, it has remained unclear whether Saudi Arabia would go ahead with such a probe, which experts say could test a system of international cooperation designed to make recommendations for safety without attempting to assign blame. The people close to the matter said Saudi Arabia had notified specialist aviation agencies abroad that it would carry out a safety investigation under international rules into flight FZ1073, which was in Saudi airspace when the co-pilot attacked the captain with an axe. One of the people, however, said it was not clear whether Saudi investigators would publish their findings. Saudi Arabia's National Transport Safety Center, which has responsibility for accident investigations, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The Saudi government and the country's regulator also did not answer requests for comment. The US National Transportation Safety Board, which would be closely involved in any probe because the Boeing 737 MAX jet that survived a steep plunge was made in the United States, confirmed it had assigned a representative to the probe. Officials in the UAE did not respond to requests for comment. Under international rules known to the industry as Annex 13, the UAE would also automatically be involved because the jet is registered there and the airline is based in Dubai. The UAE has already opened a separate criminal investigation into the incident, which its prosecutor general [USN:L1N45R06N TEXT:"has called a "terrorist attack"]." Israel, whose citizens made up nearly all the 172 people on board, has offered to take part in any Saudi-led safety investigation but has not so far been invited to join, Ofer Vaknin, director of the Aircraft Safety Investigation Authority, told Reuters. However, he added that Israel may not need to join, because it was not an operational or safety issue with the aircraft. REDUCTION IN ACCIDENTS Saudi Arabia and Israel have no diplomatic ties, though experts say the decades-old UN-backed system of cooperation on safety has demonstrated it can work across geopolitical lines. The Annex 13 rulebook grants observer status to countries with significant fatalities or injuries, but does not describe what happens where all passengers escape injury as in this case. By avoiding questions of blame and focusing solely on technical matters, air accident investigations are widely credited with sharply reducing accidents in recent decades. They have generally stayed below the diplomatic radar, allowing specialists to cooperate regardless of diplomatic ties. In 2020, despite heightened tensions following the shooting down of a Ukrainian jet by Iran, aviation officials from the US and Iran jointly took part in the playback of cockpit tapes at the offices of France's BEA agency, participants said. However, there has been growing friction in recent years over access to evidence between civil and judicial probes. In 2015, France's BEA agency went ahead with a civil safety probe after clashing with prosecutors over access to evidence following the pilot-suicide crash of a Germanwings jet. Safety officials say that whereas prosecutors take the lead when a crime is suspected, even cases of deliberate action can yield lessons on topics like recruitment or cockpit safety.

item.title: Wall Street cierra a la baja y se aleja de récords por el alza de los rendimientos en EEUU
item.description: Wall Street cerró a la baja el miércoles, en paralelo a una subida de los rendimientos de los bonos de largo plazo del Tesoro estadounidense, lo que avivó el temor a la inflación y a un aumento de la deuda, un día después de que el S&P 500 y el Nasdaq alcanzaron máximos históricos de cierre.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Culp, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
item.content:encoded: Wall Street cerró a la baja el miércoles, en paralelo a una subida de los rendimientos de los bonos de largo plazo del Tesoro estadounidense, lo que avivó el temor a la inflación y a un aumento de la deuda, un día después de que el S&P 500 y el Nasdaq alcanzaron máximos históricos de cierre. Los tres principales índices bursátiles estadounidenses cerraron con ligeras caídas, y el S&P 500 y el Dow rompieron una racha alcista de cuatro días. El Nasdaq cayó por primera vez en seis días. El índice Russell 2000 de pequeña capitalización (.RUT) tuvo un desempeño peor que el de sus pares de mayor capitalización. El crudo Brent superó brevemente los 100 dólares por barril y el rendimiento del bono del Tesoro a 30 años alcanzó un máximo en 24 años, lo que pesaba sobre los mercados bursátiles. La preocupación por el suministro, relacionada con la guerra en Irán, ha provocado una subida vertiginosa de los precios del petróleo, lo que a su vez ha reavivado el temor a la inflación y ha elevado la probabilidad de un ciclo largo de alzas de tasas de interés de los bancos centrales. Las preocupaciones, junto a los crecientes niveles de deuda corporativa y soberana, han provocado una ola de ventas de bonos a nivel mundial, lo que ha sacudido los mercados globales en las últimas semanas. Las acciones recortaron pérdidas después de que los precios del crudo bajaron tras un acuerdo de la Agencia Internacional de la Energía para acelerar la liberación de reservas de petróleo, dando prioridad al diésel. Según datos preliminares, el S&P 500 (.SPX) perdió 17,78 puntos, o un 0,23%, a 7.801,15 unidades, mientras que el Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) bajó 66,50 puntos, o un 0,24%, a 27.533,39. El Promedio Industrial Dow Jones (.DJI) cayó 355,91 puntos, o un 0,69%, 51.165,37 unidades. A raíz de la subida de los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de referencia, la tasa de interés fija de las hipotecas a 30 años se disparó la semana pasada a un máximo de casi tres años, según la Asociación de Banqueros Hipotecarios. El sector inmobiliario (.HGX) y las constructoras (.SPCOMHOME) registraron caídas del 2,3% y el 2,9%, respectivamente.

item.title: Flávio defende fim da reeleição, redução da maioridade penal e mudanças na reforma tributária por meio de PECs
item.description: O senador e candidato à Presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) afirmou nesta quarta-feira que pretende, se eleito, propor ao Congresso mudanças na Constituição para promover uma reforma do Poder Judiciário, acabar com a reeleição, reduzir a maioridade penal e mudar pontos da reforma tributária.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O senador e candidato à Presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) afirmou nesta quarta-feira que pretende, se eleito, propor ao Congresso mudanças na Constituição para promover uma reforma do Poder Judiciário, acabar com a reeleição, reduzir a maioridade penal e mudar pontos da reforma tributária. Em entrevista na porta do comitê de campanha ao lado de aliados do União Brasil e do PP, que decidiram apoiá-lo no segundo turno, Flávio disse que várias Propostas de Emenda à Constituição (PECs) poderão ser aprovadas com o novo Congresso eleito. "Tem que haver sim uma reforma do Judiciário. Sou a favor da diminuição da maioridade penal há bastante tempo, tem que ser por PEC. Tem pontos da reforma tributária que tem que ser alterada por PEC. O fim da reeleição. Eu fiz um compromisso de não concorrer à reeleição. É o Congresso que vai definir os critérios se vai ser mandato de 4 ou 5 anos, se vai valer só para presidente", afirmou. "Qualquer coisa diferente disso é especulação", ressaltou. As declarações do presidenciável, que terminou o primeiro turno das eleições à frente do presidente e candidato à reeleição Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), ocorreram um dia após Flávio ter dito que pretende aproveitar a nova composição do Congresso para fazer mudanças na Constituição, sem ter especificado quais. REFORMA TRIBUTÁRIA Falando a jornalistas, Flávio citou "aspectos da reforma tributária" entre as medidas que pretende perseguir se eleito. Lula sancionou em 2023 uma aguardada reformulação do sistema de tributação sobre o consumo, que começará a entrar em vigor no próximo ano, consolidando diversos tributos em um Imposto sobre Valor Agregado (IVA) administrado nas esferas federal e regional. "É claro que sou favorável à modernização do nosso sistema tributário, que é realmente complexo demais", afirmou o candidato. Ele argumentou, porém, que a alíquota efetiva do IVA da reforma -- estimada de forma independente em cerca de 28%, mas ainda não definida pelo governo -- seria elevada demais. Flávio Bolsonaro também reafirmou que buscará reduzir os encargos sobre a folha de pagamento e garantir que "uma parcela maior da renda dos trabalhadores brasileiros fique com eles, e não com o governo". SPLIT PAYMENT Na terça-feira, a principal assessora econômica da campanha, Daniella Marques, disse ao blog do jornalista Claudio Dantas que um eventual governo Flávio Bolsonaro eliminaria "com certeza" o mecanismo de "split payment" da reforma, pelo qual os tributos sobre o consumo são automaticamente transferidos ao governo no momento da transação, em vez de serem recolhidos posteriormente pelas empresas. Enquanto defensores do sistema afirmam que ele ampliaria a conformidade tributária e reduziria a evasão fiscal, Marques argumentou que o modelo drenaria o capital de giro das empresas. Ela também disse que um governo Flávio Bolsonaro revisaria uma ampla gama de medidas tributárias adotadas sob Lula, incluindo o imposto sobre dividendos que entrou em vigor em janeiro. Marques observou que o governo anterior de Jair Bolsonaro, pai de Flávio, havia proposto tributar dividendos apenas em conjunto com uma redução dos impostos sobre as empresas. A assessora também prometeu eliminar o imposto de 12% sobre as exportações de petróleo bruto introduzido neste ano pelo governo Lula para ajudar a financiar medidas de alívio tributário sobre combustíveis em meio à disparada global dos preços do petróleo ligada ao conflito entre Estados Unidos, Israel e Irã, classificando a cobrança como uma "aberração". Ela citou ainda a reversão dos aumentos do Imposto sobre Operações Financeiras (IOF) incidentes sobre operações de crédito corporativo, transações de câmbio e determinados investimentos em previdência privada.

item.title: Pharma lobby sues Trump administration over Medicare drug price cuts
item.description: The pharmaceutical industry's top lobby group on Wednesday sued to invalidate the Trump administration's efforts to benchmark US drug prices to lower costs overseas in the Medicare health insurance program, arguing that it is an illegal government overreach.
item.dc:creator: Michael Erman
item.content:encoded: The pharmaceutical industry's top lobby group on Wednesday sued to invalidate the Trump administration's efforts to benchmark US drug prices to lower costs overseas in the Medicare health insurance program, arguing that it is an illegal government overreach. The GLOBE rule intends to set hospital drug prices for Medicare patients. Its final version was published last week on exactly how a "most-favored-nation" pricing system based on what is paid in a group of comparable countries would be integrated in the Medicare Part B program. [USN:L1N45N0WX TEXT:"The rule"] is expected to have limited reach. CMS plans to waive it for manufacturers that have signed separate voluntary deals with the White House to cut prices for their drugs, and it could ultimately apply to as few as four drugmakers. The PhRMA lobby group filed its lawsuit in the US District Court for the District of Columbia against Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the US Department of Health and Human Services he runs, and the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services and two of its officials. The lobby group argues in its lawsuit that CMS, Medicare's regulator, has stretched the authority of a program to test new pricing ideas into rewriting Medicare's pricing structure without congressional action. Congress has given CMS "a little bit of authority to test models," PhRMA General Counsel Jim Stansel said in an interview. "Instead, CMS is doing exactly what Congress has declined to do multiple times over the last several years, and that's to replace the pricing structure in Medicare with a most-favored-nation structure." Stansel said that the lawsuit was important even with the limited reach of the rule because GLOBE could outlast the voluntary deals drugmakers have signed, and could extend to future administrations beyond Trump. Rachel Turow, an attorney with Skadden who is not involved in the lawsuit, said it can be viewed as an attempt to stop future price controls using similar mechanisms. If they don't foreclose the idea that you can use this process "to impose drug pricing controls, then they've basically opened the floodgates," Turow said. Medicare is the US government program that provides health coverage to about 70 million people aged 65 and older or with disabilities. The Department of Health and Human Services was not immediately available to comment on the lawsuit. In the finalized version of the rule, however, the agency argued that it was not overstepping its bounds, writing, "CMS is acting within a detailed, purpose specific statutory framework that Congress designed precisely for this type of model test." Trump has already signed deals with more than two dozen drugmakers, including many of the world's largest, such as Pfizer (PFE.N) , Eli Lilly (LLY.N) and Novo Nordisk (NOVOb.CO) . The final rule sharply reduced the government's projected savings from the model. HHS now estimates the program will reduce Medicare Part B spending by about $440 million over the 7-year model period, compared with roughly $11.9 billion projected in the proposed rule published last year. In 2020, PhRMA [USN:L1N2J324Z TEXT:"successfully sued"] to block a previous incarnation of most-favored-nation pricing, but that rule was invalidated on procedural grounds because the administration had rushed it out without giving the public a chance to comment. Also named in the suit were CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz, the agency's innovation center that is running the most-favored-nation pricing pilot and the director of that division, Abe Sutton.

item.title: Belgian student protests against education costs echo France
item.description: Hundreds of students, inspired in part by student unrest in neighbouring France, have taken to the streets of the eastern Belgian city of Liège, with local media reporting 107 arrests in recent days.
item.dc:creator: Bart Biesemans, Charlotte Van Campenhout
item.content:encoded: Hundreds of students, inspired in part by student unrest [USN:L1N45T0B2 TEXT:"in neighbouring France"], have taken to the streets of the eastern Belgian city of Liège, with local media reporting 107 arrests in recent days. Authorities have advised shopkeepers to close their businesses early, warning of riots. "Major unrest is underway. Close your businesses", Belgium's official government warning system BE-Alert said on Thursday. Liège's main train station was also closed but later reopened, local media reported, and police urged people to avoid the city centre. "Due to the ongoing demonstration, avoid the city centre. Traffic there is severely disrupted", the police said on social media platforms. Local authorities could not immediately be reached to confirm the arrests, which the Belga news agency reported were linked to offences including property damage and arson. Students have protested over Belgium's French-language education system, citing rising education costs, overcrowded classrooms and difficulties accessing study materials. They held signs with slogans including "It's a mess, we are fighting for a right! Not a privilege!" and "I chose education, not the hunger games!!". The unrest follows June clashes between protesters and police in Brussels over education reforms, including a tuition increase for most students in Belgium's French-speaking Community to €1,194 ($1,280) from €835. Videos circulating on social media in recent days showed shattered glass, fires and hundreds of mostly young protesters in Liège, while other footage showed police blocking roads. During Wednesday's protest, police were seen checking students for weapons. IN TOUCH WITH FRENCH STUDENTS Some students told Reuters they were in touch with French counterparts. "We support each other because we're facing pretty much the same issues," 19-year-old student Alfred said. Amelia Di Salve, also 19, who is studying to become a teacher, said Belgium's student movement began earlier this year and was reignited after students saw the demonstrations in France. "When we saw nothing was changing without protests, we decided we would start ... France did influence us a little," she said. Liège mayor Willy Demeyer told Belgian broadcaster RTBF he hoped calm would return and "that dialogue can be established and that the young people can express their grievances in a peaceful way and, if possible, have those concerns heard".

item.title: Lebanon's Hezbollah gets $200 million from Iran to help displaced, sources say
item.description: Hezbollah has received $200 million from Iran to help Lebanese displaced by this year’s war with Israel, two people with direct knowledge of the transfer said, in what would be the first significant aid from the group to supporters who bore the brunt of the conflict.
item.dc:creator: Laila Bassam, Maya Gebeily
item.content:encoded: Hezbollah has received $200 million from Iran to help Lebanese displaced by this year’s war with Israel, two people with direct knowledge of the transfer said, in what would be the first significant aid from the group to supporters who bore the brunt of the conflict. The US disputed the claim. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said in a statement that the money "is not there," accusing Hezbollah of "trying to save face with fake stories about cash influxes from Iran." A Treasury spokesperson said Iran was “running out of money and ways to move money” and that Tehran “does not have money to fund its campaign of terror.” [USN:L1N42A08R TEXT:"Hezbollah"] received the cash last month despite a tightening US economic [USN:L8N44N1OO TEXT:"chokehold"] on Iran and increasing difficulties in getting funds to Tehran's Lebanese ally, said the people. Intermediaries who moved the money charged a 20% fee, reflecting the risks of dealing with the group, they said. One said this was four times the normal fee. Asked for comment, a Hezbollah official said an amount had been secured and a plan for distributing it would be announced in the coming days, without elaborating on the source of the funds. The Iranian foreign ministry, Iran's permanent mission in Geneva, and the Lebanese government did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Israel’s bombardment and invasion of Lebanon [USN:L8N4241VG TEXT:"uprooted "]hundreds of thousands of Hezbollah’s Shi’ite Muslim constituents after the group entered the regional war in support of Iran on March 2. But those displaced have so far received little to no assistance from Hezbollah, an armed group founded by Iran’s Revolutionary Guards in 1982 which has suffered heavy Israeli blows in two wars since 2024 and is designated a terrorist group by Washington. The State Department's Pigott said Hezbollah had caused misery for Lebanese and had itself been decimated, while its backer Tehran was suffering under a US blockade of oil exports. "The United States will continue to strangle Hezballah's finances through sanctions while supporting the ability of Lebanon's legitimate government to rebuild the South," Pigott said. AIDING 50,000 FAMILIES Hezbollah would use the funds to pay an initial $3,000 per family, and priority would go to those whose villages have been destroyed or are inaccessible due to Israeli occupation, the sources said. These number around 50,000 families, one of the sources said. Iran has maintained financial support to Hezbollah through years of crippling US sanctions: it transferred $1 billion to the group in the first 10 months of 2025, according to the US Treasury Department. Tehran has never acknowledged financing Hezbollah. Iran's policy of funding regional proxies has stirred domestic protester anger against the clerical rulers in the past and could prove particularly sensitive at a time of [USN:L6N45K0UX TEXT:"worsening hardship in Iran"]. Iran had [USN:L8N42P09O TEXT:"promised Hezbollah"] more funding after Tehran signed an interim deal with Washington in June that allowed Iran to sell its oil, Reuters reported at the time. That agreement collapsed in July. Washington has since intensified economic pressure on Iran, tightening sanctions and imposing a naval blockade to block Iranian oil exports. Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem said in a speech last month that the group would soon contribute to a project aimed at housing thousands of people displaced by the war, using “available resources and donations”, without elaborating. Hezbollah's ability to fund local services and provide post-conflict aid has helped shore up its support in the past. Following a war with Israel in 2006, the group immediately handed out large cash payments to those impacted and moved swiftly to help rebuild Beirut's southern suburbs, a stronghold. But this time there has been little sign of reconstruction. Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said last month that the total reconstruction costs from the two wars since 2024 could exceed $27 billion. A COSTLY WAR The two sources provided no details on how the money got to Lebanon. One of them said it was increasingly difficult for Hezbollah to move funds via financial companies that once processed such transfers. Such firms based in Iraq and Dubai were no longer an option, and they were also now under pressure in Turkey, this source said. Hezbollah’s foes believed money was currently the group’s “oxygen”, the source added. Despite the difficulties securing funding, the group had not stopped paying its fighters and the family members of those killed in combat, this source said. In Lebanon, the war has inflicted a heavy price on the Shi’ite Muslim community from which Hezbollah draws support. Israel has razed villages across a swathe of territory it has seized in the south, saying it aims to shield northern Israel from Hezbollah attack. Israeli attacks in Lebanon have killed more than 4,300 people since March 2, according to Lebanon’s health ministry. Its toll does not say how many combatants may be among the dead. Hezbollah has not disclosed figures on its war dead. Reuters reported on May 4 that several thousand Hezbollah fighters had been killed in the war.

item.title: Pfizer to cut around 330 jobs in Italy
item.description: Pfizer will cut around 330 jobs in Italy at its Sicily plant, labour unions said on Wednesday, making the US drugmaker the latest international company downsizing its Italian operations.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pfizer (PFE.N) will cut around 330 jobs in Italy at its Sicily plant, labour unions said on Wednesday, making the US drugmaker the latest international company downsizing its Italian operations. Talks in Rome between Pfizer and Italy's industry ministry late on Tuesday did not yield results, the CGIL, CISL and UIL unions said in a statement. Pfizer's Sicily plant currently has 550 employees, unions said. Pfizer was not immediately available for comment. Italy's industry ministry said "the points raised during the meeting serve as a starting point for strengthening the dialogue," adding that industry minister Adolfo Urso would visit the plant on October 23. Further talks between Pfizer and the ministry are scheduled for November 10, the ministry added. Earlier this week, appliance maker Electrolux (ELUXb.ST) [USN:L1N45R0PJ TEXT:"presented"] a scaled-down restructuring plan for its Italian operations, with around 1,250 jobs now expected to be made redundant. Swedish telecoms equipment maker Ericsson (ERICb.ST) also said on Monday that, following talks with the ministry, a collective layoff of 131 workers in Genoa would be dropped in favour of a voluntary restructuring plan.

item.title: Petrobras, Prio e Equinor arrematam áreas no pré-sal em busca de sinergias com seus ativos
item.description: Sete blocos exploratórios de petróleo e gás no pré-sal foram arrematados nesta quarta-feira em leilão do governo brasileiro, um número recorde para vendas de áreas na importante região produtora, com empresas como a Petrobras, Prio e a norueguesa Equinor buscando garantir ativos próximos de onde já operam.
item.dc:creator: Marta Nogueira, Rodrigo Viga Gaier
item.content:encoded: Sete blocos exploratórios de petróleo e gás no pré-sal foram arrematados nesta quarta-feira em leilão do governo brasileiro, um número recorde para vendas de áreas na importante região produtora, com empresas como a Petrobras, Prio e a norueguesa Equinor buscando garantir ativos próximos de onde já operam. A portuguesa Galp e as chinesas Sinopec e CNOOC também arremataram áreas, em um certame que foi marcado pela ausência de disputas pelos blocos. Outros seis blocos ofertados não tiveram interesse, em um sinal de que parte do mercado considera que as áreas com maior potencial no pré-sal já foram comercializadas pelo governo brasileiro. Algumas das vencedoras, por outro lado, arremataram áreas onde podem aproveitar conhecimentos já adquiridos por elas na região e ainda possíveis sinergias para a exploração e produção, segundo as petroleiras. Essa situação também acabou gerando menos disputas no leilão. A operação com maior ágio da rodada em relação ao mínimo exigido foi registrada no bloco Rodocrosita, na Bacia de Santos, arrematado pelo consórcio formado pela Equinor e a portuguesa Galp, o que ressalta as sinergias buscadas no certame. O bloco Rodocrosita, comprado com oferta de excedente em óleo de 15,52% para a União -- um ágio de 494,64% -- fica próximo ao campo de Bacalhau, também operado pela norueguesa, disse a vice-presidente de Gestão de Ativos da Equinor no Brasil, Leticia Andrade, a jornalistas. "É uma área que a gente já conhece ou está conhecendo cada vez mais, conforme a produção do campo (de Bacalhau) vai avançando. E aí, existe sempre uma possibilidade de potencial sinergia, potencialmente entre Rodocrosita e Bacalhau", disse a executiva. Já em Rubi, também arrematado pela Equinor na Bacia de Santos, com oferta de 25,02% de excedente em óleo e ágio de 91,72%, "existe uma possibilidade de ser um desenvolvimento independente", disse a executiva, pontuando que ainda é "muito cedo" para dizer. "Agora, dada a vitória, vamos fazer as análises para decidir que rumo tomar." 'TIEBACK' FUNCIONA BEM O presidente da Pré-Sal Petróleo SA (PPSA), empresa que representa a União nos contratos de partilha de produção no pré-sal, Luis Paroli, ressaltou que houve um recorde de áreas arrematadas em um mesmo leilão do pré-sal, e confirmou a estratégia das empresas sobre a busca por ativos onde já atuam e conhecem. "Foi muito positivo o leilão, é um recorde, na verdade; nunca aconteceu de sair sete áreas no mesmo leilão. É um recorde para partilha e também os ágios foram muito bons, então a nossa avaliação é que foi um grande sucesso", disse o executivo a jornalistas, após o certame. Paroli pontuou ainda que o Brasil tem áreas com potencial "gigantesco" no pré-sal, se comparado com o mundo. Porém ponderou que há necessidade de que sejam campos grandes para que sejam viabilizados economicamente, já que estão em águas ultraprofundas. "Hoje, como a gente não tem aqueles grandes campos, as pessoas que estão próximas ali, que já têm o FPSO funcionando... talvez o potencial não seja para 'standalone', não seja suficiente, mas para um 'tieback' funciona e funciona muito bem, e dá uma margem muito boa. O que explica também os ágios", disse Paroli. PETROBRAS E PRIO Na mesma linha, a Petrobras (PETR3.SA) arrematou os blocos Azurita, na Bacia de Campos, e Cruzeiro do Sul, na Bacia de Santos, oferecendo percentuais de excedente em óleo de 30,0% e 15,27%, respectivamente. Os ágios em relação ao excedente mínimo de óleo alcançaram 139,81% em Azurita e 8,07% em Cruzeiro do Sul, segundo dados da ANP. "O resultado está dentro das oportunidades e, as áreas, junto de outros blocos (onde Petrobras já atua)", disse a diretora de Exploração e Produção, Sylvia Anjos, à Reuters. De acordo com o geólogo consultor da Zag Consultoria Pedro Zalán, Azurita fica próximo aos campos da Petrobras de Espadarte e Tartaruga Verde, que produzem no pós-sal. "Azurita foi adquirida por seus méritos próprios... é uma área com alto potencial para uma grande descoberta no pré-sal", disse o especialista à Reuters. Já Cruzeiro do Sul, segundo Zalán, foi adquirido para fazer sinergia com o futuro desenvolvimento do campo gigante de Júpiter, que fica logo ao norte da área. "Júpiter é uma gigantesca acumulação de óleo, condensado e gás, mas tem uma quantidade muito alta de CO2 (75%)... Cruzeiro do Sul é a continuação das reservas de Júpiter, e ele é necessário para tornar econômico o desenvolvimento de Júpiter", afirmou. A brasileira Prio foi a vencedora dos blocos Magnetita e Hematita, ambos na Bacia de Campos. Em Magnetita, a empresa ofertou excedente em óleo de 32,8% para a União, com ágio de 132,79%, enquanto em Hematita apresentou proposta de 7,18%, equivalente a ágio de 315,03%. Os blocos adquiridos pela Prio são localizados ao norte da Bacia de Campos, próximos aos campos da companhia de Wahoo e Frade, disse a empresa em comunicado. "A companhia avaliará os recursos prospectivos dos blocos, que em caso de sucesso poderão ser objeto de desenvolvimento através de 'tieback' ao FPSO Valente, localizado no campo de Frade", disse a Prio. O bloco Jade foi vencido pelo consórcio formado pelas chinesas CNOOC e Sinopec, com oferta de 18,2% de excedente em óleo para a União, representando ágio de 65,76%, com os chineses realizando sua "primeira grande aventura exploratória no pré-sal como operadores, e não mais como meros sócios da Petrobras", disse o geólogo. Os blocos Turmalina, Larimar, Aragonita, Opala, Granada e Cerussita não receberam oferta. O leilão resultou em uma arrecadação total de R$530,47 milhões em bônus fixos de assinatura à União, que também levou dos arrematantes o direito de parte do petróleo a ser produzido no futuro. O investimento exploratório previsto nas áreas somou R$778,43 milhões, de acordo com o balanço apresentado pela Agência Nacional do Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis (ANP).

item.title: Halozyme wins court order to block Merck's injected Keytruda in select European markets
item.description: Biopharma company Halozyme said on Wednesday that a Dutch patent court ruled in its favor against Merck , ordering the drugmaker to halt the manufacture and sale of injectable Keytruda in eight European markets.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Biopharma company Halozyme (HALO.O) said on Wednesday that a Dutch patent court ruled in its favor against Merck (MRK.N) , ordering the drugmaker to halt the manufacture and sale of injectable Keytruda in eight European markets. Here are some details: Halozyme said a specialized Dutch patent court in The Hague found that Merck had infringed one of its patents covering MDASE, Halozyme's technology for rapid, high-volume under-the-skin drug delivery. The court ordered Merck to stop the production and sale of injectable Keytruda in Belgium, Denmark, France, Ireland, Italy, Sweden, Switzerland and the Netherlands. The drugmaker has been counting on the simpler-to-use subcutaneous version of the drug, known as Keytruda SC, to help drive growth as key patents on its original intravenous version expire later in the decade. "We strongly disagree with the Dutch court's decision to grant a cross-border injunction. We consider Halozyme's patent to be invalid globally and its allegation of infringement to be without merit," a Merck spokesperson said in a statement. The company said it is evaluating next steps. Halozyme has also sued Merck for patent infringement in the US, alleging the under-the-skin formulation of Keytruda infringes 15 patents that Halozyme has filed since 2011. The company sued Merck in Germany and was granted a preliminary injunction last year, stopping Merck's launch of Keytruda SC in Germany.

item.title: Euro cae hacia mínimos de 17 meses, dólar mantiene ganancias tras minutas Fed
item.description: El euro cayó el miércoles, ya que los bonos franceses sufrieron nuevas presiones por preocupaciones fiscales, mientras el dólar mantuvo sus ganancias tras la publicación de las minutas de la última cita de la Reserva Federal.
item.dc:creator: Chuck Mikolajczak
item.content:encoded: El euro cayó el miércoles, ya que los bonos franceses sufrieron nuevas presiones por preocupaciones fiscales, mientras el dólar mantuvo sus ganancias tras la publicación de las minutas de la última cita de la Reserva Federal. * El retorno de los bonos de Francia y España aumentó y el de los países más endeudados registró un alza más pronunciada que el de activos de refugio como los alemanes, a medida que persisten las preocupaciones fiscales en Francia y los precios del crudo retoman protagonismo. * El rendimiento del bono francés a 10 años se disparó 11,9 puntos básicos, en su mayor aumento diario en dos semanas, al 4,8696%, mientras que el de su par alemán se mantuvo sin cambios en el 3,4805%. * "Lo que ocurre en Europa es que, durante un tiempo, han funcionado un poco al estilo del Estado del bienestar, gastando mucho dinero sin generar realmente muchos ingresos, y eso finalmente les está pasando factura", dijo Juan Pérez, de Monex USA en Washington. * "Si a esto le sumamos que todo el mundo ha tenido que gastar más dinero en energía, las perspectivas no son buenas. La atención se centra en Europa, y el panorama es muy, muy negativo", agregó. * El euro perdió un 0,53%, a 1,1198 dólares, cerca de los mínimos de 17 meses registrados el lunes. * El índice dólar , que compara al billete verde con una cesta de seis destacadas divisas, ganó un 0,32%, a 102,24 unidades; tras recortar brevemente sus ganancias, volvió a repuntar después de conocerse las minutas de la Fed. * Las actas revelaron que los responsables de política monetaria estaban divididos el mes pasado sobre los motivos para subir las tasas. "Algunos participantes" consideraban necesaria un alza para contener el impacto de los choques en los precios de la energía y otros bienes, mientras que un grupo más partidario de una política restrictiva la veía necesaria para prevenir una inflación emergente impulsada por la demanda. * El dólar también se vio respaldado por la persistencia de unos precios energéticos elevados, si bien el petróleo perdió las ganancias iniciales en una sesión volátil, después de que la Agencia Internacional de la Energía acordara acelerar la liberación de reservas de crudo y priorizar el diésel para combatir los precios récord del combustible. * Mientras, la libra esterlina restó un 0,42%, a 1,3216 dólares, pero alcanzó su nivel más alto desde junio de 2025 ante el euro. Frente al yen , el dólar cedió un 0,09%, a 157,95 unidades.

item.title: France suspends use of stun grenades to police student protests
item.description: The French government said on Wednesday it was pausing the use of stun grenades in its policing of student protests, after a 15-year-old boy's hand was blown off during a clash with riot police, fuelling protesters' accusations of police brutality.
item.dc:creator: Makini Brice, Janis Laizans
item.content:encoded: The French government said on Wednesday it was pausing the use of stun grenades in its policing of [USN:L1N45S0C7 TEXT:"student protests"], after a 15-year-old boy's [USN:L1N45R08Q TEXT:"hand was blown off"] during a clash with riot police, fuelling protesters' accusations of police brutality. Protests showed no sign of easing, with more than 500 schools closed a day after demonstrations swept across the country, and unions representing high-school students, teachers and other workers planning more marches for Thursday. The wave of protests has been going on for more than two weeks and has exposed widespread public anger six months ahead of an election to replace President Emmanuel Macron. Speaking to the nation on Wednesday evening, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said the government would review the demands made by students and present proposals at the end of October on issues ranging from renovating buildings to make more teachers available, but gave no details. "In the past, too many promises were not kept, quite simply because they were untenable," Lecornu said. "What I want are concrete, quick and fully funded answers." The lack of an immediate government response, which was decried by student leaders after talks at the education ministry earlier on Wednesday, appeared unlikely to quell the protests. At Lycee Lamartine, a high school in central Paris, protesters sang the Marseillaise, chanted slogans and performed Mexican waves as they blockaded the entrance to the school. "We saw there were lots of crumbling walls, a shortage of teachers in public schools, absent teachers," said Gabriel Fillieule, who used to attend a public school but now goes to a private one. He and others said they were protesting to demand better learning conditions for all. POLICE'S USE OF FORCE BEING INVESTIGATED While most of Wednesday's blockades were peaceful, police used tear gas and pushed back protesters in a street barricaded by rubbish bins outside Sciences Po university in central Paris. Rights groups, labour unions, students and some opposition politicians have accused the police of using disproportionate force to quell the wave of protests. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said he had ordered the suspension of the use of stun grenades following an incident in the northern city of Lens on Monday in which there was a "strong possibility" the firing of a stun grenade had caused a teenager to lose his hand. "I am suspending their use for the high-school students' movement until light has been shed on what happened in this case," said the minister, who added that 18 incidents in total had been referred to the police inspectorate for investigation. Protesters have said they blame poor learning conditions for a sharp drop in French teenagers' scores in reading and maths over the past decade. French 15-year-olds scored 43 points lower in reading in 2025 than in 2015, according to the OECD's Programme for International Student Assessment, the biggest drop among the OECD countries. Their maths scores also dropped the most. But the government, under pressure to tame public debt amid weak growth, has little spare cash to address students' complaints of teacher shortages, ageing school buildings and inequalities between schools in affluent and poor areas. TWENTY-FOUR HIGH SCHOOLS DAMAGED BY FIRE OR VANDALISM Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has acknowledged the "legitimate" demands of France's students but also described the unrest as the most violent student demonstrations in decades. Education Minister Edouard Geffray told parliament that 24 high schools had been damaged by fire or vandalism to the extent that they would remain closed for weeks, meaning some 30,000 students would receive no in-person teaching until they reopened. He estimated it would cost €20 million to €30 million ($22 million to $34 million) to fix the damage. Far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen, the frontrunner according to opinion polls, said those who damaged schools should pay for the repairs rather than taxpayers. The government has adopted a similar stance and has a bill going through parliament that aims to set up such a system. According to an Elabe poll for BFM TV, 72% of French people think the students' demands are legitimate, but 55% of them think the protests should stop. UNREST ELSEWHERE Elsewhere in Europe, where budgets have been under pressure as governments respond to successive cost-of-living and energy crises, students in parts of Belgium staged similar protests. In the Belgian city of Liege in the southern French-speaking Wallonia region, at least 107 people have been arrested in connection with student protests this month, the Belga news agency reported. Teachers are also on strike. In Portugal, the main teachers' union FENPROF launched an indefinite strike in mid-September over working conditions, with teachers refusing to do any unpaid work beyond the 35 hours a week mandated by law. And in Spain, teachers' unions have been protesting conditions in state schools. Teachers in Madrid plan a strike on October 14 to press demands including a reduction in hours, smaller class sizes and higher salaries. ($1 = 0.8952 euros)

item.title: Five more UK rate-rigging convictions quashed as SFO prosecutions unravel
item.description: Five former Barclays traders, jailed in Britain for plotting to rig global benchmark interest rates, won an appeal to clear their names on Wednesday, further unravelling some of the UK Serious Fraud Office's most high-profile prosecutions.
item.dc:creator: Kirstin Ridley
item.content:encoded: Five former Barclays (BARC.L) traders, jailed in Britain for plotting to rig global benchmark interest rates, won an appeal to clear their names on Wednesday, further unravelling some of the UK Serious Fraud Office's most high-profile prosecutions. London's Court of Appeal quashed the [USN:L8N3YU25P TEXT:"convictions"] of Philippe Moryoussef, from France, Kolkata-born Jay Merchant, Britons Colin Bermingham and Jonathan Mathew, and Alex Pabon, an American. The traders were cast by prosecutors as a symbol of banker greed at a time of taxpayer fury at eye-watering bank bailouts following the 2007-2009 credit crisis, which sent stock markets plunging and pitched economies into recession. But the men applied to clear their names after the Supreme Court last year [USN:L8N3TK0IL TEXT:"overturned"] the convictions of [USN:L1N3W9013 TEXT:"Tom Hayes"] — a former star UBS (UBSG.S) and Citigroup (C.N) trader — and ex-Barclays peer Carlo Palombo for rigging now-defunct interbank interest rate Libor and its euro equivalent, Euribor. The Supreme Court ruled that the trial judges had misdirected juries and that legal errors undermined the fairness of the trials, laying the groundwork for Wednesday's appeals. "All five convictions were rendered unsafe by the same series of errors ... For those reasons, all five convictions will be quashed," the Court of Appeal said. TEARFUL TRADER SAYS DECISION HARD TO TAKE IN Merchant, Pabon, Moryoussef, Bermingham and Mathew were convicted of conspiracy to defraud and sentenced to between 33 months and 8 years in jail between 2016 and 2019 after a series of landmark SFO trials. "It's hard to take in," said a tearful Bermingham, 70, outside the courtroom. "You don't believe it until you hear it." Moryoussef, now 58, gained notoriety for jumping bail and fleeing to France. He was tried in London in his absence, sentenced to eight years and has remained a fugitive since. "Today, I am regaining my soul, and for the first time, I can envision my next chapter in peace," he said in a statement. Pabon, 48, noted: "Ten years ago, my jury was told, as a matter of law, that an honest answer to the Libor question was not a defence. The Serious Fraud Office now accepts my conviction is unsafe." The SFO reiterated that the Supreme Court had found "ample evidence" on which a properly directed jury could have convicted Hayes and Palombo. But it added: "After carefully considering this judgment and the full circumstances, we do not oppose the appeals of five individuals convicted by juries in relation to Libor and Euribor." A further attempted appeal by Christian Bittar, a French former Deutsche Bank (DBKGn.DE) trader sentenced to jail in 2018, is expected to be heard on Friday. Bittar, once dubbed one of the world's most skilled traders, is the only appellant whose case is being contested by the SFO following his guilty plea more than eight years ago. Designed to estimate the costs at which banks would lend to each other, Libor and Euribor were once a benchmark for interest rates underpinning around $450 trillion of financial contracts, from derivatives to student loans.

item.title: Barril cae tras acuerdo de la AIE de acelerar la liberación de reservas
item.description: Los precios del petróleo cayeron el miércoles, después de que la Agencia Internacional de la Energía acordara acelerar la liberación de reservas y dar prioridad al gasóleo, en un intento por frenar los precios récord de los combustibles, mientras la guerra en Irán reduce el suministro mundial.
item.dc:creator: Georgina Mccartney
item.content:encoded: Los precios del petróleo cayeron el miércoles, después de que la Agencia Internacional de la Energía acordara acelerar la liberación de reservas y dar prioridad al gasóleo, en un intento por frenar los precios récord de los combustibles, mientras la guerra en Irán reduce el suministro mundial. * Los futuros del Brent bajaban 0,5 dólares, o un 0,5%, a 100,08 dólares por barril, mientras que el West Texas Intermediate en Estados Unidos (WTI) caía 1,18 dólares, o un 1,32%, a 88,26 dólares. * La AIE señaló que llevar a cabo lo antes posible las liberaciones anunciadas anteriormente podría aportar unos 100 millones de barriles al mercado, aunque analistas y algunos gobiernos indicaron que esa cifra no representaba necesariamente una nueva intervención de tal magnitud. * Francia liberará 10 millones de barriles de gasóleo de sus reservas estratégicas, informó el miércoles la emisora Franceinfo, citando fuentes anónimas. * "Europa es el epicentro de toda esta crisis de suministro (...) y estas liberaciones abordan ese problema y alivian en cierta medida la presión sobre la demanda de WTI. Esto debería reducir parte de la presión sobre los suministros estadounidenses", afirmó John Kilduff, socio de Again Capital. * Las reservas de crudo en Estados Unidos cayeron en 3,2 millones de barriles a 424,1 millones de barriles en la semana que finalizó el 2 de octubre, según la Administración de Información de Energía (EIA), frente a las previsiones de los analistas en una encuesta de Reuters, que apuntaban a un aumento de 1,7 millones de barriles. * Según Tamas Varga, analista de PVM, los inversores no están convencidos de que los recientes aumentos de la oferta y las exportaciones procedentes de Oriente Medio sean sostenibles. * La presión a la baja sobre los precios remitió debido a la proximidad de la tormenta en Estados Unidos, así como a los conflictos en Oriente Medio y Ucrania, señaló Varga. * Los hutíes de Yemen atacaron el miércoles el aeropuerto internacional de Adén con misiles balísticos y drones cargados de explosivos, según informó el Ministerio de Transporte del país, mientras se intensifican los combates entre el grupo alineado con Irán y las fuerzas gubernamentales respaldadas por Arabia Saudita. * Ucrania atacó el miércoles dos instalaciones petroleras rusas, mientras que Rusia bombardeó Ucrania con oleadas de misiles y drones, lo que provocó la muerte de al menos 15 personas, según informaron las autoridades ucranianas. * Los ataques contra la infraestructura energética rusa y la pérdida de capacidad de refino en Oriente Medio han tensado los mercados de combustible, afirmó el martes el presidente ejecutivo de Vitol, Russell Hardy. * En Estados Unidos, meteorólogos afirmaron el martes que una tormenta que se está formando en el golfo de México se convertirá en el primer huracán del Atlántico de 2026 en un plazo de dos días. Las zonas marítimas situadas en la trayectoria de la tormenta producen el 15% del crudo estadounidense y el 5% del gas natural del país.

item.title: Life sciences firm Danaher to launch AI-powered autonomous research lab in 2027
item.description: Life sciences company Danaher said on Wednesday it plans to launch its first AI-powered autonomous research lab early next year to make drug discovery and development faster and more efficient.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Life sciences company Danaher (DHR.N) said on Wednesday it plans to launch its first AI-powered autonomous research lab early next year to make drug discovery and development faster and more efficient. Here are more details: The lab, projected to operate at scale in early 2027, will combine AI, robotics and technologies from several Danaher operating companies in one connected workflow to develop custom antibodies and other molecular tools It is expected to make discovering molecules eight times faster and unlock a tenfold increase in generating target-binding molecules annually "That frees them (scientists) to focus on the complex scientific challenges where human insight matters most," said JC Gutierrez-Ramos, chief science officer of Danaher The lab uses AI to help create new molecules that can bind specifically to a biological target, including antibodies, then builds and tests each one, feeding every result back into the model to improve the next design The lab is an example of a broader program across Danaher, intended to create a fleet of smart instruments, the company said

item.title: US 30-year mortgage rate hits highest in nearly three years
item.description: The interest rate on the most common US home loan jumped last week to its highest in almost three years, worsening affordability for buyers four weeks before elections that will decide if President Donald Trump's Republicans keep control of Congress.
item.dc:creator: Ann Saphir
item.content:encoded: The interest rate on the most common US home loan jumped last week to its highest in almost three years, worsening affordability for buyers four weeks before elections that will decide if President Donald Trump's Republicans keep control of Congress. The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage surged 19 basis points to 7.49% in the week ended October 2, the Mortgage Bankers Association said on Wednesday. It was last higher in November 2023. Mortgage rates are tied closely to the yield on US 10-year Treasury notes, which earlier this week [USN:L8N45T0F3 TEXT:"hit a 24-year high"], driven by worries over inflationary pressures from soaring oil prices and data showing stronger US economic growth. The cost of living is the top issue on Americans' minds as they decide how they will vote on November 3, a Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday showed, and is one reason why Trump's [USN:L6N45R10Y TEXT:"approval rating"] is at a record low of 32%. Home borrowing rates are up about 1.4 percentage points since joint US-Israeli strikes against Iran began in late February, tracking a similar rise in the 10-year Treasury yield, which topped 5.3% on Monday. Inflation is also on the rise, registering 3.4% in August by a measure that the Federal Reserve targets at 2%. Fed policymakers have signaled they expect to follow their September interest-rate increase with another rate hike by year's end, though markets are for now betting they will not move at their upcoming policy meeting at the end of October. Asked by a reporter Wednesday about mortgage rates, Trump called Fed chairman Kevin Warsh "great," but added the rest of the board "would like to see the country do badly, in my opinion, because I think interest rates should come down." US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, in the Oval Office with Trump, blamed inflation and high mortgage rates on the temporary shock from higher oil prices. "So once we get on the other side of this Iran conflict, (the) energy market is going to be well supplied, and we will move down towards the Fed's target and mortgage rates and the 10-year will come back down," Bessent said. Mortgage loan applications fell 4.2% last week from the previous week, the MBA said on Wednesday, with refinancing applications dropping sharply. Overall application volumes are the lowest since February 2025 and have fallen nearly 50% since January. "Very few homeowners have an incentive to refinance at these rates, and the jump in borrowing costs has caused many potential borrowers to step back from the purchase market," said Joel Kan, the MBA’s deputy chief economist.

item.title: UPS to hire 100,000 temporary workers for holiday season
item.description: United Parcel Service on Wednesday said it would hire 100,000 seasonal employees across the US, as it prepares for a spike in parcel volumes for the upcoming holiday season.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: United Parcel Service (UPS.N) on Wednesday said it would hire 100,000 seasonal employees across the US, as it prepares for a spike in parcel volumes for the upcoming holiday season. Here are some details: The holiday season is the busiest period for parcel delivery companies, during which daily volumes tend to double. Shippers and most retailers boost the hiring of temporary workers during the period from late November to early January. The seasonal workers will help sort, move and deliver packages during the holiday rush, UPS said. The parcel delivery company hired 125,000 holiday season staff in 2024, but did not provide a comparable hiring number last year. In January, the company said it would cut [USN:L4N3YS10F TEXT:"up to 30,000 operational jobs"] and close 24 facilities in 2026 in a bid to scale down shipments for its largest customer, Amazon, and shift towards more profitable shipments.

item.title: Wall Street ends lower, off record highs, as Treasury yields climb
item.description: Wall Street closed lower on Wednesday, as long-dated US Treasury yields resumed their climb, reviving fears about inflation and mounting debt the day after the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq hit record closing highs.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Culp, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
item.content:encoded: Wall Street closed lower on Wednesday, as long-dated US Treasury yields resumed their climb, reviving fears about inflation and mounting debt the day after the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq hit record closing highs. All three major US stock indexes were modestly lower, with the S&P 500 and the Dow snapping four-day winning streaks. The Nasdaq notched its first down day in six. The small-cap Russell 2000 (.RUT) underperformed its larger cap counterparts, dropping 1.3%. In the wake of Tuesday's stock market rally, Brent crude settled above $100 per barrel and long-dated Treasury yields touched a [USN:L8N45T0F3 TEXT:"24-year high"]. Iran war-related [USN:L1N45T02U TEXT:"supply concerns"] have led to soaring oil prices, which in turn have revived inflation worries and raised the chances of a prolonged central bank rate hiking cycle. Those concerns, combined with mounting corporate and sovereign debt levels, have caused a global bond selloff, which rattled global markets in recent weeks. Investors "have been looking for some relief on oil, which would drive some relief on rates and that would therefore help the stock market," said Thomas Martin, senior portfolio manager at GLOBALT in Atlanta. "The third quarter was supposed to be the weak quarter of the year; we were supposed to get a correction," Martin added. "That didn't happen, so it's three cheers and let's take some money off the table." Stocks pared losses after [USN:L1N45T02U TEXT:"crude prices"] turned lower following the International Energy Agency's agreement to speed up the release of oil stocks, prioritizing diesel.
